title.zh: 卷七十三 列傳第二十三: 薛收 姚思廉 顏師古 令狐德棻 孔穎達
title.en: Volume 73 Biographies 23: Xue Shou, Yao Silian, Yan Shigu, Linghu Defen, Kong Yingda
title.raw: 卷七十三 列傳第二十三: 薛收 姚思廉 顏師古 令狐德棻 孔穎達 Volume 73 Biographies 23: Xue Shou, Yao Silian, Yan Shigu, Linghu Defen, Kong Yingda

sentences.zh: 薛收 兄子元敬 收子元超 從子稷

translations.literal: Xue Shou; his elder cousin's son Yuanjing; Shou's son Yuanchao; his younger cousin's son Ji
translations.idiomatic: Xue Shou; Yuanjing, son of his elder cousin; Yuanchao, Shou's son; Ji, son of a younger cousin

sentences.zh: 姚思廉 顏師古 弟相時

translations.literal: Yao Silian; Yan Shigu; his younger brother Xiangshi
translations.idiomatic: Yao Silian; Yan Shigu; and his younger brother Xiangshi

sentences.zh: 令狐德棻 鄧世隆 顧胤 李延壽 李仁實等附

translations.literal: Linghu Defen; Deng Shilong; Gu Yin; Li Yanshou; Li Renshi and others appended
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Defen; Deng Shilong; Gu Yin; Li Yanshou; Li Renshi; with others appended

sentences.zh: 孔穎達 司馬才章 王恭馬嘉運等附

translations.literal: Kong Yingda; Sima Caizhang; Wang Gong, Ma Jiayun, and others appended
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yingda; Sima Caizhang; Wang Gong and Ma Jiayun; with others appended

sentences.zh: 薛收，字伯褒，蒲州汾陰人，隋內史侍郎道衡子也。

translations.literal: Xue Shou, style name Bobao, was a man of Fenyin in Puzhou, and was the son of Xue Daoheng, Interior Secretary of the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Shou, courtesy name Bobao, came from Fenyin in Puzhou and was the son of the Sui Interior Secretary Xue Daoheng.

sentences.zh: 事繼從父孺以孝聞。

translations.literal: He served his successor uncle Ru and was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He attended upon his uncle Xue Ru, who had succeeded to the family line, and won renown for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 年十二，解屬文。

translations.literal: At age twelve he understood literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: By the age of twelve he was already skilled at writing.

sentences.zh: 以父在隋非命，乃潔志不仕。

translations.literal: Because his father had met an untimely death under the Sui, he therefore kept his will pure and would not serve in office.
translations.idiomatic: After his father died an unnatural death under the Sui, he resolved to hold himself apart and refused to enter government service.

sentences.zh: 大業末，郡舉秀才，固辭不應。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era the commandery recommended him as xiucai; he firmly declined and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daye reign, the commandery nominated him as a xiucai candidate, but he steadfastly refused to accept.

sentences.zh: 義旗起，遁於首陽山，將協義舉。

translations.literal: When the righteous banner was raised, he fled to Mount Shouyang, intending to join in the righteous rising.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel cause was raised, he withdrew to Mount Shouyang, planning to take part in the uprising.

sentences.zh: 蒲州通守堯君素潛知收謀，乃遣人迎收所生母王氏置城內，收乃還城。

translations.literal: Yao Junsu, Tongshou of Puzhou, secretly learned of Shou's plot, and therefore sent men to welcome Shou's birth mother Lady Wang into the city; Shou then returned to the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Junsu, the Puzhou Tongshou, learned of Shou's plans in secret and had his birth mother Lady Wang brought into the city, whereupon Shou came back inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 後君素將應王世充，收遂逾城歸國。

translations.literal: Later, when Junsu was about to respond to Wang Shichong, Shou then crossed the wall and returned to the [Tang] state.
translations.idiomatic: When Junsu was on the verge of siding with Wang Shichong, Shou climbed over the city wall and defected to the Tang cause.

sentences.zh: 秦府記室房玄齡薦之於太宗，即日召見，問以經略，收辯對縱橫，皆合旨要。

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling, Recorder of the Prince of Qin's household, recommended him to Emperor Taizong; that same day he was summoned for an audience and questioned on strategy; Shou replied at length in every direction, all in accord with the essential intent.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling, secretary of the Prince of Qin's household, recommended him to the future Taizong, who summoned him the same day and questioned him on strategy; Shou answered expansively on every point, each reply hitting the mark.

sentences.zh: 授秦府主簿，判陝東道大行台金部郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Clerk of the Prince of Qin's household and concurrently served as Langzhong of the Revenue Section of the Grand Secretariat of the Eastern Shaanxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief clerk of the Prince of Qin's establishment and also acted as director of the revenue section on the Eastern Shaanxi grand secretariat staff.

sentences.zh: 時太宗專任征伐，檄書露布，多出於收。

translations.literal: At that time Taizong devoted himself wholly to campaigns; proclamations and battlefield bulletins mostly came from Shou.
translations.idiomatic: While the Prince of Qin was absorbed in military campaigns, most of the manifestos and victory announcements issued in his name were drafted by Shou.

sentences.zh: 言辭敏速，還同宿構，馬上即成，曾無點竄。

translations.literal: His words were swift and keen, as though composed overnight; on horseback they were finished at once, never needing a single revision.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was quick and sharp, as if he had composed it long in advance; he could finish a piece on horseback without changing a single character.

sentences.zh: 太宗討王世充也，竇建德率兵來拒，諸將皆以為宜且退軍，以觀賊形勢。

translations.literal: When Taizong attacked Wang Shichong, Dou Jiande led troops to oppose him; the generals all thought it best to withdraw the army for a time and observe the enemy's situation.
translations.idiomatic: During Taizong's campaign against Wang Shichong, Dou Jiande marched to block him; the generals all urged a temporary withdrawal to gauge the enemy's strength.

sentences.zh: 收獨建策曰：「世充據有東都，府庫填積，其兵皆是江淮精銳，所患者在於乏食，是以為我所持，求戰不可。

translations.literal: Shou alone proposed a plan, saying: "Shichong holds the Eastern Capital; the storehouses are piled full; his troops are all elite forces of the Jianghuai region; what afflicts him is lack of food—therefore he is held in our grasp, and he cannot seek battle.
translations.idiomatic: Shou alone urged a different course: "Shichong holds the Eastern Capital with overflowing treasuries, and his soldiers are the finest troops of the Jianghuai. His weakness is hunger, which keeps him in our grip—he cannot afford to offer battle.

sentences.zh: 建德親總軍旅，來拒我師，亦當盡彼驍雄，期於奮決。

translations.literal: Jiande personally commands the army and comes to oppose our forces; he too will surely deploy all his fierce champions, expecting a decisive clash.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande is leading his army in person to block us; he too will throw his best fighters into the field, bent on a decisive fight.

sentences.zh: 若縱其至此，兩寇相連，轉河北之糧以相資給，則伊、洛之間戰鬥不已。

translations.literal: If we let him reach this place, the two foes will link together and shift Hebei grain to supply each other; then between the Yi and Luo rivers fighting will never cease.
translations.idiomatic: If we allow him to join Shichong here, the two enemies will link up and shuttle Hebei grain between them, and war around the Yi and Luo will never end.

sentences.zh: 今宜分兵守營，深其溝防，即世充欲戰，慎勿出兵。

translations.literal: Now we should divide troops to guard the camps and deepen the ditches and defenses; even if Shichong wishes to fight, take care not to send troops out.
translations.idiomatic: We should detach forces to hold our camps and deepen our trenches and defenses; even if Shichong tries to provoke a battle, we must not sally forth.

sentences.zh: 大王親率猛銳，先據成皋之險，訓兵坐甲，以待其至。

translations.literal: Your Highness should personally lead the fierce elite, first seize the perilous ground at Chenggao, drill the troops and sit in armor, and await his arrival.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness should lead our crack troops in person, seize the defiles at Chenggao first, keep the men drilled and armored, and wait for him to arrive.

sentences.zh: 彼以疲弊之師，當我堂堂之勢，一戰必克。

translations.literal: They with weary and spent troops will meet our grand and imposing force; one battle will surely conquer.
translations.idiomatic: His exhausted army will meet our full strength in the field, and we are sure to win in a single engagement.

sentences.zh: 建德即破，世充自下矣。

translations.literal: Once Jiande is broken, Shichong will submit of himself.
translations.idiomatic: Break Jiande, and Shichong will collapse on his own.

sentences.zh: 不過兩旬，二國之君，可面縛麾下。

translations.literal: In no more than twenty days the rulers of the two states can be bound face to face beneath your banners.
translations.idiomatic: Within twenty days both enemy kings can be brought before you with their hands tied.

sentences.zh: 若退兵自守，計之下也。」

translations.literal: If we withdraw the army and merely defend ourselves, that is the inferior plan."
translations.idiomatic: To pull back and stand on the defensive would be the worst option."

sentences.zh: 太宗納之，卒擒建德。

translations.literal: Taizong accepted it and in the end captured Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong adopted his plan and in the end took Jiande prisoner.

sentences.zh: 東都平，太宗入觀隋氏宮室，嗟後主罄人力以逞奢侈。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital was pacified, Taizong entered to view the Sui palaces and sighed that the Last Emperor had exhausted human strength to indulge luxury.
translations.idiomatic: After the Eastern Capital fell, Taizong toured the Sui palaces and lamented how the last Sui emperor had squandered the nation's labor on extravagance.

sentences.zh: 收進曰：「竊聞峻宇雕牆，殷辛以滅；

translations.literal: Shou advanced and said: "I have heard that lofty halls and carved walls caused Xin of Yin to perish;
translations.idiomatic: Shou stepped forward and said, "I have heard it said that towering halls and carved walls brought down King Zhou of Shang;

sentences.zh: 土階茅棟，唐堯以昌。

translations.literal: earthen steps and thatched beams caused Tang Yao to flourish.
translations.idiomatic: while earthen steps and thatched roofs made Emperor Yao prosper.

sentences.zh: 秦帝增阿房之飾，漢後罷露台之費，故漢祚延而秦禍速，自古如此。

translations.literal: The Qin emperor added the adornment of Epang; the Han empress dowager abolished the expense of the Terrace Pavilion; therefore the Han mandate endured while Qin disaster came swiftly—thus it has been since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor of Qin lavished ornament on Epang Palace, while Empress Dowager Wen of Han cut the cost of the Terrace Pavilion; the Han house endured while Qin ruin came quickly—so it has always been.

sentences.zh: 後主曾不能察，以萬乘之尊，困一夫之手，使土崩瓦解，取譏後代，以奢虐所致也。」

translations.literal: The Last Emperor could not perceive this; with the dignity of the Son of Heaven he was trapped in a single man's hands, causing the realm to crumble and dissolve, drawing mockery from later ages—all because of extravagance and cruelty."
translations.idiomatic: The last Sui emperor never saw this lesson: a ruler who commanded ten thousand chariots was brought low by a single man, his realm crumbling to ruin and his name a byword for later ages—all because of luxury and cruelty."

sentences.zh: 太宗悅其對。

translations.literal: Taizong was pleased with his reply.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was delighted with his answer.

sentences.zh: 及軍還，授天策府記室參軍。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed Recorder-Adjutant of the Heavenly Strategies Office.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned, he was made recorder-adjutant of the Heavenly Strategies Office.

sentences.zh: 太宗初授天策上將、尚書令，命收與世南並作第一讓表，竟用收者。

translations.literal: When Taizong was first appointed General of Heavenly Strategies and Director of the Department of State Affairs, he ordered Shou and Yu Shinan each to draft the first memorial of refusal; in the end Shou's was used.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong was first made General of Heavenly Strategies and Director of the Department of State Affairs, he had both Shou and Yu Shinan draft the first memorial declining the honors; Shou's version was the one adopted.

sentences.zh: 太宗曾侍高祖游後園中，獲白魚，命收為獻表，收援筆立就，不復停思，時人推其二表贍而速。

translations.literal: Taizong once attended Gaozu on a tour of the rear garden and caught a white fish; he ordered Shou to compose a presentation memorial; Shou took up the brush and finished at once without pausing to think; men of the time praised both his memorials as ample yet swift.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while attending Gaozu on a stroll through the rear garden, Taizong caught a white fish and asked Shou to write the presentation memorial; Shou wrote it straight off without a pause for thought, and contemporaries admired both pieces for their fullness and speed.

sentences.zh: 從平劉黑闥，封汾陰縣男。

translations.literal: He followed in the pacification of Liu Heita and was enfeoffed as Baron of Fenyin County.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in suppressing Liu Heita and was ennobled as Baron of Fenyin County.

sentences.zh: 武德六年，以本官兼文學館學士，與房玄齡、杜如晦特蒙殊禮，受心腹之寄。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wude, while retaining his original post he also served as Academician of the Literature Hall; together with Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui he received special courtesy and was entrusted as a confidant.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 6 he was also made a scholar of the Literature Hall while keeping his existing post; he, Fang Xuanling, and Du Ruhui were treated with exceptional honor and entrusted as inner confidants.

sentences.zh: 又嘗上書諫獵，太宗手詔曰：「覽讀所陳，實悟心膽，今日成我，卿之力也。

translations.literal: He also once submitted a memorial remonstrating against hunting; Taizong wrote in his own hand: "Having read what you set forth, I am truly enlightened in heart and gall; what I am today, your strength has made it.
translations.idiomatic: He once memorialized against hunting, and Taizong replied in his own hand: "Reading what you wrote has truly opened my eyes; what I have become today is largely your doing.

sentences.zh: 明珠兼乘，豈比來言，當以誡心，書何能盡！

translations.literal: Bright pearls together with four-horse teams—how can they compare with your recent words? I should take them as admonition to the heart; how can writing express it all!
translations.idiomatic: Jewels and teams of four horses are nothing beside what you have just said; I shall take your words to heart, though no letter could say enough!

sentences.zh: 今賜卿黃金四十鋌，以酬雅意。」

translations.literal: Now I bestow on you forty ingots of gold to repay your refined intent."
translations.idiomatic: I now grant you forty ingots of gold in recognition of your thoughtful counsel."

sentences.zh: 七年，寢疾，太宗遣使臨問，相望於道。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he took to his bed with illness; Taizong sent envoys to inquire in person, one after another along the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he fell gravely ill; Taizong sent one envoy after another to visit him, so that they seemed to pass each other on the road.

sentences.zh: 尋命輿疾詣府，太宗親以衣袂撫收，論敘生平，潸然流涕。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered brought in his litter to the princely residence; Taizong personally stroked Shou with his sleeve, recounted their shared life, and shed tears profusely.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was carried by litter to the prince's mansion; Taizong himself took Shou's sleeve in his hand, spoke of their years together, and wept openly.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年三十三。

translations.literal: Soon after he died, aged thirty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward, at the age of thirty-three.

sentences.zh: 太宗親自臨哭。

translations.literal: Taizong personally came to mourn and weep.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong came in person to mourn him.

sentences.zh: 哀慟左右。

translations.literal: His grief moved those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: His grief moved everyone around him.

sentences.zh: 與收從父兄子元敬書曰：「吾與卿叔共事，或軍旅多務，或文詠從容。

translations.literal: He wrote to Yuanjing, son of Shou's father's cousin's elder brother, saying: "I served together with your uncle; sometimes amid the many tasks of army and camp, sometimes at ease in literary song.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Yuanjing, Shou's cousin, saying, "Your uncle and I worked side by side—sometimes buried in military affairs, sometimes at leisure over poetry.

sentences.zh: 何嘗不驅馳經略，款曲襟抱？

translations.literal: When did we not gallop through strategy and open our hearts in intimate warmth?
translations.idiomatic: We never ceased to debate strategy or speak frankly from the heart.

sentences.zh: 比雖疾苦，日冀痊除，何期一朝，忽成萬古！

translations.literal: Recently, though he suffered illness, day by day I hoped for recovery—who expected that in a single morning it would suddenly become ten thousand ages!
translations.idiomatic: Lately, though he was ill, I looked each day for his recovery—who could have thought that in a single morning he would be gone forever?

sentences.zh: 追尋痛惋，彌用傷懷。

translations.literal: Looking back in pain and regret, my wounded heart grows only deeper.
translations.idiomatic: The more I look back, the sharper my grief becomes.

sentences.zh: 且聞其兒子幼小，家徒壁立，未知何處安置？

translations.literal: Moreover I hear his son is still young and the household has nothing but bare walls—I do not know where they can be settled?
translations.idiomatic: I hear too that his son is still small and the family has nothing left but bare walls—where are they to find a home?

sentences.zh: 宜加安撫，以慰吾懷。」

translations.literal: You should add comfort and reassurance to ease my heart."
translations.idiomatic: See that they are cared for, to ease my mind."

sentences.zh: 因使人弔祭，贈物三百段。

translations.literal: He therefore sent men to offer condolences and sacrifices, bestowing three hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to offer condolences and sacrifices, with a gift of three hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 及後，遍圖學士等形像。

translations.literal: Later, portraits were painted of all the academicians and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Later, portraits were painted of all the scholars of the hall.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘆曰：「薛收遂成故人，恨不早圖其像。」

translations.literal: Taizong sighed and said: "Xue Shou has become an old friend indeed; I regret that I did not paint his likeness earlier."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sighed and said, "Xue Shou is already among the departed; I regret that we did not paint his portrait sooner."

sentences.zh: 及登極，顧謂房玄齡曰：「薛收若在，朕當以中書令處之。」

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne he turned to Fang Xuanling and said: "If Xue Shou were still alive, I would place him in the post of Director of the Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: After he took the throne he said to Fang Xuanling, "If Xue Shou were still alive, I would have made him Director of the Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 又嘗夢收如平生，又敕有司特賜其家粟帛。

translations.literal: He also once dreamed of Shou as in life, and again ordered the authorities specially to bestow grain and cloth on his family.
translations.idiomatic: He once dreamed of Shou as if he were still alive, and again ordered the authorities to grant his family a special allotment of grain and cloth.

sentences.zh: 貞觀七年，贈定州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenguan he was posthumously made Governor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 7 he was posthumously appointed Governor of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 永徽六年，又贈太常卿，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yonghui he was further posthumously made Minister of Imperial Rites and buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 6 he was further posthumously made Minister of Imperial Rites and granted burial near Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 文集十捲。

translations.literal: His collected writings were ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to ten juan.

sentences.zh: 元敬，隋選部侍郎邁子也。

translations.literal: Yuanjing was the son of Mai, Vice Minister of the Selection Bureau of the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing was the son of the Sui Vice Minister of the Selection Bureau, Xue Mai.

sentences.zh: 有文學，少與收及收族兄德音齊名，時人謂之「河東三鳳」。

translations.literal: He had literary learning; in youth he was famed equally with Shou and Shou's clansman elder brother Deyin; men of the time called them "the Three Phoenixes of Hedong."
translations.idiomatic: A man of letters, in youth he was ranked with Shou and Shou's clansman Deyin; contemporaries called them "the Three Phoenixes of Hedong."

sentences.zh: 收為長雛，德音為鸑鷟，元敬以年最小為鹓雛。

translations.literal: Shou was the eldest fledgling, Deyin the yu'luo, and Yuanjing, being youngest in years, was the yuan fledgling.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was called the eldest phoenix chick, Deyin the yu'luo phoenix, and Yuanjing, as the youngest, the yuan phoenix chick.

sentences.zh: 武德中，元敬為秘書郎，太宗召為天策府參軍，兼直記室。

translations.literal: During Wude, Yuanjing was Secretary Gentleman; Taizong summoned him as Adjutant of the Heavenly Strategies Office and concurrently Direct Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wude era Yuanjing served as a secretary; Taizong summoned him as an adjutant of the Heavenly Strategies Office and also made him a direct recorder.

sentences.zh: 收與元敬俱為文學館學士。

translations.literal: Shou and Yuanjing were both Academicians of the Literature Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Both Shou and Yuanjing served as scholars of the Literature Hall.

sentences.zh: 時房、杜等處心腹之寄，深相友托，元敬畏於權勢，竟不之狎，如晦常云：「小記室不可得而親，不可得而疏。」

translations.literal: At that time Fang, Du, and others held the trust of confidants and were deeply bound in friendship; Yuanjing stood in awe of their power and in the end did not become intimate with them. Ruhui often said: "The young recorder cannot be drawn close, nor can he be kept distant."
translations.idiomatic: Fang, Du, and the others were inner confidants and close allies; Yuanjing respected their power too much to grow familiar with them. Du Ruhui often said, "That young recorder is neither someone you can cozy up to nor someone you can afford to alienate."

sentences.zh: 太宗入東宮，除太子舍人。

translations.literal: When Taizong entered the Eastern Palace, Yuanjing was appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong became crown prince, Yuanjing was made an attendant in the heir's household.

sentences.zh: 時軍國之務，總於東宮，元敬專掌文翰，號為稱職。

translations.literal: At that time military and state affairs were concentrated in the Eastern Palace; Yuanjing alone managed documents and was said to fulfill his duties fittingly.
translations.idiomatic: Military and state affairs were then centered in the Eastern Palace, and Yuanjing alone handled the paperwork; he was reckoned fully equal to the task.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon after he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 收子元超。

translations.literal: Shou's son Yuanchao.
translations.idiomatic: Shou's son, Yuanchao.

sentences.zh: 元超早孤，九歲襲爵汾陰男。

translations.literal: Yuanchao was orphaned early; at nine he inherited the title Baron of Fenyin.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchao lost his father while still young; at nine he inherited the barony of Fenyin.

sentences.zh: 及長，好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: When grown he loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew up he became devoted to study and excelled at writing.

sentences.zh: 太宗甚重之，令尚巢剌王女和靜縣主，累授太子舍人，預撰《晉書》。

translations.literal: Taizong greatly valued him, had him marry the Princess of Hejing, daughter of Prince Li of Chao, repeatedly appointed him Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and had him take part in compiling the Book of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong held him in high regard, gave him the Princess of Hejing, daughter of Prince Li of Chao, in marriage, repeatedly appointed him attendant to the heir, and enrolled him in the compilation of the Book of Jin.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，擢拜給事中，時年二十六。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne he was promoted and appointed Supervising Censor; he was then twenty-six.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong came to the throne he was promoted to supervising censor at the age of twenty-six.

sentences.zh: 數上書陳君臣政體及時事得失，高宗皆嘉納之。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials setting forth the political order between ruler and minister and the gains and losses of current affairs; Gaozong praised and accepted them all.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized on the proper relation between ruler and minister and on current affairs; Gaozong welcomed and adopted his advice.

sentences.zh: 俄轉中書舍人，加弘文館學士，兼修國史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat, added as Academician of the Hongwen Hall, and concurrently edited the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made drafting attendant of the Secretariat, also appointed a Hongwen Hall scholar, and put in charge of editing the national history.

sentences.zh: 中書省有一盤石，初，道衡為內史侍郎，嘗踞而草制，元超每見此石，未嘗不泫然流涕。

translations.literal: In the Secretariat there was a flat boulder; in the beginning, when Daoheng was Interior Secretary, he had once sat upon it to draft edicts; whenever Yuanchao saw this stone he never failed to shed tears profusely.
translations.idiomatic: In the Secretariat there stood a flat stone on which his grandfather Daoheng, as Interior Secretary, had once sat to draft edicts; whenever Yuanchao passed it he wept.

sentences.zh: 永徽五年，丁母憂解。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yonghui he completed mourning for his mother and left office.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 5 he left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 明年，起授黃門侍郎，兼檢校太子左庶子。

translations.literal: The next year he was recalled and appointed Vice Director of the Gate, and concurrently Acting Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled to serve as vice director of the Gate Department and also as acting left assistant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 元超既擅文辭，兼好引寒俊，嘗表薦任希古、高智周、郭正一、王義方、孟利貞等十餘人，由是時論稱美。

translations.literal: Yuanchao was skilled in literary phrasing and also loved to advance men of humble talent; he once memorialized recommending more than ten men including Ren Xigu, Gao Zhizhou, Guo Zhengyi, Wang Yifang, and Meng Lizhen; therefore contemporary opinion praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchao was gifted in letters and fond of promoting talented men from modest backgrounds; he once recommended more than a dozen scholars, including Ren Xigu, Gao Zhizhou, Guo Zhengyi, Wang Yifang, and Meng Lizhen, and won praise in public opinion.

sentences.zh: 後以疾出為饒州刺史。

translations.literal: Later, because of illness he went out to serve as Governor of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on account of illness, he was sent out as governor of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜東台侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Vice Director of the Eastern Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of his tenure he was appointed vice director of the Eastern Terrace.

sentences.zh: 右相李義府以罪配流巂州，舊制，流人禁乘馬，元超奏請給之，坐貶為簡州刺史。

translations.literal: The Right Chancellor Li Yifu was sentenced for crime and exiled to Xizhou; by old regulation exiles were forbidden to ride horses; Yuanchao memorialized requesting that horses be granted him; for this he was demoted to Governor of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the right chancellor Li Yifu was exiled to Xizhou for his crimes, Yuanchao memorialized that he be allowed horses, contrary to the usual rule for exiles; for this Yuanchao was demoted to governor of Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，西台侍郎上官儀伏誅，又坐與文章款密，配流巂州。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Shangguan Yi, Vice Director of the Western Terrace, was executed; Yuanchao was again implicated for intimate literary friendship with him and was sentenced to exile in Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, when Shangguan Yi of the Western Terrace was executed, Yuanchao was punished again for his close literary ties with him and exiled to Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 上元初，遇赦還，拜正諫大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shangyuan, he met an amnesty and returned, and was appointed Rectifier Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shangyuan era he was recalled under an amnesty and appointed rectifier remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷中書侍郎，尋同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat, and soon after made of the Third Rank, co-equal with the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made vice director of the Secretariat and soon afterward chancellor of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 時高宗幸溫泉校獵，諸蕃酋長亦持弓矢而從。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozong went to the hot springs for a hunting review, and the chieftains of the various foreign peoples also bore bows and arrows and followed.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong went to the hot springs for a hunting expedition, the tribal chieftains of the frontier peoples also followed with bows at the ready.

sentences.zh: 元超以為既非族類，深可為虞，上疏切諫，帝納焉。

translations.literal: Yuanchao thought that since they were not of our kindred, this was deeply to be feared; he submitted a stern memorial of remonstrance, and the emperor accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchao argued that these men were not of our own people and that the situation was deeply alarming; he submitted a forceful memorial of remonstrance, and the emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 時元超特承恩遇，常召入與諸王同預私宴。

translations.literal: At that time Yuanchao especially received imperial favor and was often summoned to join the princes in private banquets.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchao enjoyed exceptional favor and was often summoned to private banquets alongside the imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 又重其文學政理之才，曾謂元超曰：「長得卿在中書，固不藉多人也。」

translations.literal: The emperor also valued his talent in letters and governance; he once said to Yuanchao: "So long as I have you in the Secretariat, I truly have no need of many others."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also prized his literary and administrative gifts and once told him, "As long as you are at the Secretariat, I hardly need anyone else."

sentences.zh: 永隆二年，拜中書令，兼太子左庶子。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonglong he was appointed Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonglong 2 he was made director of the Secretariat and also left assistant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 高宗幸東都，太子於京師監國，因留元超以侍太子。

translations.literal: Gaozong went to the Eastern Capital; the Heir Apparent remained in the capital to oversee the state, and therefore Yuanchao was left behind to attend the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong went to the Eastern Capital, the crown prince stayed in Chang'an to oversee the realm, and Yuanchao was left behind to assist him.

sentences.zh: 帝臨行謂元超曰：「朕之留卿，如去一臂。

translations.literal: As the emperor was about to depart he said to Yuanchao: "In leaving you behind, it is as though I were losing an arm.
translations.idiomatic: As he was leaving, the emperor told Yuanchao, "Keeping you here feels like losing an arm.

sentences.zh: 但吾子未閒庶務，關西之事，悉以委卿。

translations.literal: Yet my son is not yet versed in the many affairs of state; all matters of the Guanxi region I wholly entrust to you.
translations.idiomatic: But my son is still inexperienced in government; I entrust all affairs of the capital region entirely to you.

sentences.zh: 所寄既深，不得默爾。」

translations.literal: The trust placed in you is so deep that you cannot remain silent."
translations.idiomatic: The responsibility I place on you is too great for you to hold your tongue."

sentences.zh: 於是元超表薦鄭祖玄、鄧玄挺、崔融為崇文館學士。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yuanchao memorialized recommending Zheng Zuxuan, Deng Xuanting, and Cui Rong as Academicians of the Chongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchao then memorialized recommending Zheng Zuxuan, Deng Xuanting, and Cui Rong as scholars of the Chongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 又數上疏諫太子，高宗知而稱善，遣使慰諭，賜物百段。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly submitted memorials remonstrating with the Heir Apparent; Gaozong learned of this and praised it, sent envoys to comfort and instruct him, and bestowed one hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent repeated memorials remonstrating with the crown prince; when Gaozong heard of this he approved, sent envoys to commend him, and granted him a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 弘道元年，以疾乞骸，加金紫光祿大夫，聽致仕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongdao, on account of illness he begged to return his bones; he was given the Grand Master of the Golden Purple Light and allowed to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongdao 1, citing illness, he asked to retire; he was promoted to grand master of the golden purple light and permitted to leave office.

sentences.zh: 其年冬卒，年六十二。

translations.literal: That winter he died, aged sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died that winter, at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈光祿大夫、秦州都督，陪葬乾陵。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Military Governor of Qinzhou, and buried with honor at Qianling.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand master for splendid happiness and military governor of Qinzhou, and granted burial near Qianling.

sentences.zh: 文集四十捲。

translations.literal: His collected writings were forty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to forty juan.

sentences.zh: 子曜，亦以文學知名，聖歷中，修《三教珠英》，官至正諫大夫。

translations.literal: His son Yao was also famed for literary learning; during the Shengli era he took part in compiling the Pearls of the Three Teachings and rose to Rectifier Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yao likewise won renown for letters; during the Shengli reign he helped compile the Pearls of the Three Teachings and rose to rectifier remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 元超從子稷。

translations.literal: Yuanchao's younger cousin's son Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchao's cousin, Ji.

sentences.zh: 稷舉進士，累轉中書舍人。

translations.literal: Ji passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly transferred until he became Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Ji passed the jinshi examination and eventually rose to drafting attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時從祖兄曜為正諫大夫，與稷俱以辭學知名，同在兩省，為時所稱。

translations.literal: At that time his elder cousin's son Yao was Rectifier Remonstrator; Ji and he were both famed for literary eloquence, serving together in the two secretariats, and were praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Yao then served as rectifier remonstrator; both men were famed for literary skill and held posts in the two secretariats, winning praise from their contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 景龍末，為諫議大夫、昭文館學士。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jinglong era he became Remonstrating Censor and Academician of the Zhaowen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Jinglong era he was made remonstrating censor and a scholar of the Zhaowen Hall.

sentences.zh: 好古博雅，尤工隸書。

translations.literal: He loved antiquity and was broadly learned, especially skilled in clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: A lover of antiquity and wide learning, he was especially accomplished in clerical script.

sentences.zh: 自貞觀、永徽之際，虞世南、褚遂良時人宗其書跡，自後罕能繼者。

translations.literal: From the Zhenguan and Yonghui period, Yu Shinan and Chu Suiliang were revered by men of the time for their calligraphic traces; after them few could follow.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Zhenguan and Yonghui reigns, Yu Shinan and Chu Suiliang had been the calligraphic models of their age, and few afterward could match them.

sentences.zh: 稷外祖魏徵家富圖籍，多有虞、褚舊跡，稷銳精模仿，筆態遒麗，當時無及之者。

translations.literal: Ji's maternal grandfather Wei Zheng's household was rich in books and records and possessed many old traces of Yu and Chu; Ji keenly imitated them, his brush manner vigorous and beautiful, and none of the time could equal him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's maternal grandfather Wei Zheng owned a great library with many works by Yu and Chu; Ji studied their hand intently until his brushwork was forceful and elegant, and none of his contemporaries could rival him.

sentences.zh: 又善畫，博探古蹟。

translations.literal: He was also skilled at painting and broadly sought out ancient traces.
translations.idiomatic: He was also a painter and a wide-ranging collector of antiquities.

sentences.zh: 睿宗在籓，留意於小學，稷於是特見招引，俄又令其子伯陽尚仙源公主。

translations.literal: When Ruizong was in his princely fief he paid attention to the lesser learning; Ji was therefore especially summoned, and soon his son Boyang was given the Princess of Xianyuan in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: While Ruizong was still a prince he took an interest in scholarship and the arts, and Ji was singled out for patronage; soon afterward Ruizong had Ji marry his son Boyang to the Princess of Xianyuan.

sentences.zh: 及踐祚，累拜中書侍郎，與蘇頲等對掌制誥。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, Ji was repeatedly appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and, together with Su Ting and others, jointly managed edicts and decrees.
translations.idiomatic: After Ruizong ascended the throne, Ji rose to vice director of the Secretariat and shared responsibility for drafting edicts with Su Ting and others.

sentences.zh: 俄與中書侍郎崔日用參知政事。

translations.literal: Soon he and Vice Director of the Secretariat Cui Riyong jointly participated in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he and Vice Director Cui Riyong were made participants in governance.

sentences.zh: 睿宗以鐘紹京為中書令，稷勸令禮讓，因入言於帝曰：「紹京素無才望，出自胥吏，雖有功勳，未聞令德。

translations.literal: Ruizong made Zhong Shaojing Director of the Secretariat; Ji urged him to yield in courtesy, and therefore entered to speak to the emperor, saying: "Shaojing has never had talent or reputation; he came from clerks and runners; though he has merit, I have not heard of fine virtue in him.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong appointed Zhong Shaojing director of the Secretariat; Ji urged Shaojing to step aside and told the emperor, "Shaojing has never had reputation or ability; he rose from the clerical ranks. Though he has rendered service, I have heard nothing of outstanding virtue in him.

sentences.zh: 一朝超居元宰，師長百僚，臣恐清濁同貫，失於聖朝具瞻之美。」

translations.literal: In a single morning he has leapt to the chief minister's place and become teacher and elder to the hundred officials; I fear the clear and the turbid will run in one channel and the holy court will lose the beauty of universal regard."
translations.idiomatic: To leap in a single day to chief minister and become mentor to the whole bureaucracy—I fear the worthy and unworthy will be treated alike and the court will lose the dignity that all should look up to."

sentences.zh: 帝然其言，因紹京表讓，遂轉為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words; through Shaojing's memorial of yielding, he was then transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed; Shaojing submitted a memorial declining the post and was transferred to minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 稷又於帝前面折崔日用，遞相短長，由是罷知政事，遷左散騎常侍，歷工部、禮部二尚書。

translations.literal: Ji also openly rebuked Cui Riyong before the emperor, each in turn exposing the other's faults; for this he was removed from participation in state affairs, transferred to Left Regular Attendant, and served successively as Minister of Works and Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Ji also openly attacked Cui Riyong before the emperor, the two men trading accusations; for this Ji was removed from governance, made left regular attendant, and later served as minister of works and minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 以翊贊睿宗功封晉國公，賜實封三百戶，除太子少保。

translations.literal: For his merit in assisting Ruizong he was enfeoffed as Duke of Jin, granted three hundred actual households, and appointed Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: For his service in supporting Ruizong he was enfeoffed as Duke of Jin with three hundred taxable households and made junior tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 睿宗常召稷入宮中參決庶政，恩遇莫與為比。

translations.literal: Ruizong often summoned Ji into the palace to participate in deciding the many affairs of state; no one's favor could be compared with his.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong often summoned Ji into the palace to help decide state affairs, and no one enjoyed greater favor.

sentences.zh: 及竇懷貞伏誅，稷以知其謀，賜死於萬年縣獄中。

translations.literal: When Dou Huaizhen was executed, Ji was punished because he had known of the plot and was granted death in the prison of Wannian County.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Huaizhen was executed, Ji was condemned for having known of the conspiracy and was ordered to take his own life in the Wannian County jail.

sentences.zh: 子伯陽，以尚公主拜右千牛衛將軍、駙馬都尉，亦以功封安邑郡公，別食實封四百戶。

translations.literal: His son Boyang, for marrying a princess, was appointed General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard and Commandant of the Horse for the Imperial Son-in-law; he was also enfeoffed for merit as Duke of Anyi Commandery, with a separate grant of four hundred actual households.
translations.idiomatic: His son Boyang, through marriage to a princess, became general of the right thousand-ox guard and commandant escorting the imperial son-in-law; for his own service he was also made Duke of Anyi with a separate income of four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 及父死，特免坐，左遷晉州員外別駕。

translations.literal: When his father died he was specially exempted from punishment by association and demoted to Acting Vice Governor of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he was spared the usual punishment for a relative's crime and demoted to acting vice governor of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋而配徙嶺表，在道自殺。

translations.literal: Soon he was sentenced to exile beyond the Ling range; on the road he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon exiled to the far south and killed himself on the way.

sentences.zh: 伯陽子談，開元十六年，尚常山公主，拜駙馬都尉、光祿員外卿，旬日暴卒。

translations.literal: Boyang's son Tan, in the sixteenth year of Kaiyuan, married the Princess of Changshan and was appointed Commandant Escorting the Imperial Son-in-law and Acting Vice Director of the Imperial Household; within ten days he died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: Boyang's son Tan married the Princess of Changshan in Kaiyuan 16, was made commandant escorting the imperial son-in-law and acting vice director of the imperial household, and died suddenly within ten days.

sentences.zh: 姚思廉，字簡之，雍州萬年人。

translations.literal: Yao Silian, style name Jianzhi, was a man of Wannian in Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Silian, courtesy name Jianzhi, came from Wannian in Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 父察，陳吏部尚書；

translations.literal: His father Cha was Minister of the Ministry of Personnel of Chen;
translations.idiomatic: His father Cha had been minister of personnel under the Chen;

sentences.zh: 入隋，歷太子內舍人、秘書丞、北絳公，學兼儒史，見重於三代。

translations.literal: entering the Sui he served successively as Attendant within the Heir Apparent's household, Secretary Aide, and Duke of Beijiang; his learning combined Confucian and historical studies, and he was esteemed through three dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: after entering Sui service he held posts including attendant in the heir's household, secretary aide, and Duke of Beijiang; versed in both classical and historical learning, he was respected across three dynasties.

sentences.zh: 陳亡，察自吳興始遷關中。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, Cha moved from Wuxing and first relocated to the Guanzhong region.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, Cha left Wuxing and moved to the Guanzhong region.

sentences.zh: 思廉少受漢史於其父，能盡傳家業，勤學寡慾，未嘗言及家人產業。

translations.literal: Silian in youth received the Han histories from his father, was able fully to transmit the family profession, studied diligently with few desires, and never spoke of the family's property.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Silian studied the Han histories under his father, inherited the family scholarly tradition in full, pursued learning with few wants, and never spoke of household wealth.

sentences.zh: 在陳為揚州主簿，入隋為漢王府參軍，丁父憂解職。

translations.literal: Under Chen he was Registrar of Yangzhou; entering the Sui he became Adjutant of the Prince of Han's household and left office upon completing mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chen he served as registrar of Yangzhou; under Sui he became an adjutant in the Prince of Han's household and left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 初，察在陳嘗修梁、陳二史，未就，臨終令思廉續成其志。

translations.literal: In the beginning, when Cha was in Chen he had once compiled the histories of Liang and Chen but did not finish; on his deathbed he ordered Silian to continue and fulfill his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while serving Chen, Cha had begun histories of Liang and Chen but left them unfinished; on his deathbed he charged Silian to complete them.

sentences.zh: 丁繼母憂，廬於墓側，毀瘠加人。

translations.literal: Upon completing mourning for his stepmother he built a hut beside the tomb; his emaciation from grief exceeded that of others.
translations.idiomatic: After his stepmother's death he built a mourning hut beside her tomb and wasted away with grief more deeply than most.

sentences.zh: 服闋，補河間郡司法書佐。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Judicial Clerk of Hejian Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was appointed judicial clerk of Hejian commandery.

sentences.zh: 思廉上表陳父遺言，有詔許其續成《梁》、《陳史》。

translations.literal: Silian submitted a memorial setting forth his father's last words; an edict permitted him to continue and complete the History of Liang and History of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Silian memorialized the court with his father's dying charge, and an edict authorized him to complete the histories of Liang and Chen.

sentences.zh: 煬帝又令與起居舍人崔祖浚修《區宇圖志》。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang also ordered him, together with Diarist Cui Zujun, to compile the Atlas and Gazetteer of the Realm.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang also had him work with diarist Cui Zujun on the Atlas and Gazetteer of the Realm.

sentences.zh: 後為代王侑侍讀。

translations.literal: Later he became Lecturer to Prince You of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He later became lecturer to Prince You of Dai.

sentences.zh: 會義師克京城，侑府僚奔駭，唯思廉侍王，不離其側。

translations.literal: When the righteous army took the capital, the prince's household officials fled in terror; only Silian attended the prince and did not leave his side.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel army seized the capital, the prince's staff fled in panic, but Silian alone remained at the prince's side.

sentences.zh: 兵將升殿，思廉厲聲謂曰：「唐公舉義，本匡王室，卿等不宜無禮於王。」

translations.literal: As the soldiers were about to ascend the hall, Silian said in a stern voice: "The Duke of Tang raised the righteous banner to restore the royal house; you ought not to be disrespectful to the prince."
translations.idiomatic: As the soldiers were about to enter the hall, Silian cried out, "The Duke of Tang took up arms to restore the imperial house; you must not treat the prince with disrespect."

sentences.zh: 眾服其言，於是布列階下。

translations.literal: The crowd accepted his words and thereupon arrayed themselves below the steps.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers accepted his rebuke and drew up in ranks below the steps.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞而義之，許其扶侑至順陽閣下，泣拜而去。

translations.literal: Gaozu heard and approved his righteousness, permitting him to support You to the foot of the Shunyang Pavilion, where he wept, bowed, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu heard of this and admired his loyalty, allowing him to escort Prince You to the Shunyang Pavilion, where Silian wept, bowed, and took his leave.

sentences.zh: 觀者咸嘆曰：「忠烈之士也。

translations.literal: Onlookers all sighed and said: "A loyal and stern man!
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers all exclaimed, "A man of loyal valor!

sentences.zh: 仁者有勇，此之謂乎！」

translations.literal: The benevolent have courage—this is what is meant!"
translations.idiomatic: The benevolent are brave—this is what they mean!"

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，授秦王文學。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Silian was appointed Literary Scholar to the Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu took the throne, Silian was appointed literary scholar to the Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 後太宗征徐圓朗，思廉時在洛陽，太宗嘗從容言及隋亡之事，慨然嘆曰：「姚思廉不懼兵刃，以明大節，求諸古人，亦何以加也！」

translations.literal: Later, when Taizong campaigned against Xu Yuanlang, Silian was then in Luoyang; Taizong once spoke at ease of the fall of the Sui and sighed with feeling: "Yao Silian did not fear blades and weapons, thereby clarifying great integrity; search among the ancients—how could one add to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Later, during Taizong's campaign against Xu Yuanlang, Silian was in Luoyang; Taizong once spoke of the fall of the Sui and sighed, "Yao Silian faced drawn swords without flinching and showed what true integrity means; among the ancients, who could surpass that?"

sentences.zh: 因寄物三百段以遺之，書曰：「想節義之風，故有斯贈。」

translations.literal: He therefore sent three hundred bolts of goods as a gift, writing: "Thinking of the wind of integrity and righteousness, therefore this gift."
translations.idiomatic: He sent him three hundred bolts of silk with a note: "Remembering your integrity, I make this gift."

sentences.zh: 尋引為文學館學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was brought in as Academician of the Literature Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed a scholar of the Literature Hall.

sentences.zh: 太宗入春宮，遷太子洗馬。

translations.literal: When Taizong entered the Eastern Palace, Silian was transferred to Groom of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong became crown prince, Silian was made groom in the heir's household.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，遷著作郎、弘文館學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was transferred to Compiler and Academician of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he became a compiler and Hongwen Hall scholar.

sentences.zh: 寫其形像，列於《十八學士圖》，令文學褚亮為之贊，曰：「志苦精勤，紀言實錄。

translations.literal: His portrait was painted and placed in the Picture of the Eighteen Academicians; the literary scholar Chu Liang was ordered to compose a eulogy, saying: "His will was bitterly diligent, his records of words truthful and real.
translations.idiomatic: His portrait was painted for the Picture of the Eighteen Scholars, and the literary scholar Chu Liang was asked to write a laudation: "Steadfast in purpose and tireless in study, truthful in recording words.

sentences.zh: 臨危殉義，餘風勵俗。」

translations.literal: Facing peril he died for righteousness; his remaining wind encourages custom."
translations.idiomatic: Facing danger he upheld righteousness; his example still stirs the world."

sentences.zh: 三年，又受詔與秘書監魏徵同撰梁、陳二史。

translations.literal: In the third year he again received an edict to compile, together with Director of the Secretariat Wei Zheng, the histories of Liang and Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was again ordered to compile the histories of Liang and Chen together with Wei Zheng, director of the imperial library.

sentences.zh: 思廉又采謝炅等諸家梁史續成父書，並推究陳事，刪益博綜顧野王所修舊史，撰成《梁書》五十捲、《陳書》三十捲。

translations.literal: Silian also gathered the Liang histories of various houses such as Xie Jiong and continued his father's book, and further investigated Chen affairs, deleting and adding and broadly synthesizing the old history compiled by Gu Yewang, completing the History of Liang in fifty juan and the History of Chen in thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: Silian drew on various Liang histories, including that of Xie Jiong, to finish his father's work, researched Chen affairs, revised and synthesized Gu Yewang's earlier history, and produced the History of Liang in fifty juan and the History of Chen in thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 魏徵雖裁其總論，其編次筆削，皆思廉之功也，賜彩絹五百段，加通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Although Wei Zheng edited the general discussions, the ordering and brushwork were all Silian's achievement; he was granted five hundred bolts of colored silk and promoted to Regular Attendant Direct and Unhindered.
translations.idiomatic: Though Wei Zheng edited the general essays, the arrangement and drafting were Silian's work; he was rewarded with five hundred bolts of silk and promoted to regular attendant direct and unhindered.

sentences.zh: 思廉以籓邸之舊，深被禮遇，政有得失，常遣密奏之，思廉亦直言無隱。

translations.literal: Because of his old ties in the princely residence Silian was deeply favored with courtesy; when government had gains or losses, the emperor often sent secret memorials to him, and Silian also spoke straight without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: As an old companion from the prince's household, Silian enjoyed exceptional favor; when policy went awry the emperor often sent him secret messages, and Silian spoke frankly without holding back.

sentences.zh: 太宗將幸九成宮，思廉諫曰：「離宮游幸，秦皇、漢武之事，固非堯、舜、禹、湯之所為也。」

translations.literal: When Taizong was about to visit the Jiucheng Palace, Silian remonstrated, saying: "Excursions to detached palaces were the ways of the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han; they are certainly not what Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang did."
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong planned to visit the Jiucheng Palace, Silian remonstrated: "Pleasure tours to detached palaces were the ways of the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han—not the ways of Yao, Shun, Yu, or Tang."

sentences.zh: 言甚切至。

translations.literal: His words were very earnest and penetrating.
translations.idiomatic: His words were forceful and pointed.

sentences.zh: 太宗諭曰：「朕有氣疾，熱便頓劇，固非情好游賞也。」

translations.literal: Taizong instructed him, saying: "I have a qi disorder; when it is hot it suddenly becomes severe; this is certainly not because I love roaming for pleasure."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong replied, "I suffer from a breathing ailment that grows acute in heat; this is not mere love of sightseeing."

sentences.zh: 因賜帛五十匹。

translations.literal: He therefore bestowed fifty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He then granted him fifty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 九年，拜散騎常侍，賜爵豐城縣男。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Regular Attendant and ennobled as Baron of Fengcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was made regular attendant and ennobled as baron of Fengcheng County.

sentences.zh: 十一年卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh year.

sentences.zh: 太宗深悼惜之，廢朝一日，贈太常卿，謚曰康，賜葬地於昭陵。

translations.literal: Taizong deeply mourned and regretted him, suspended court for one day, posthumously made him Minister of Imperial Rites, gave the posthumous name Kang, and granted burial land at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong mourned him deeply, suspended court for a day, posthumously made him minister of imperial rites with the posthumous name Kang, and granted him burial land near Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 子處平，官至通事舍人。

translations.literal: His son Chuping rose to Master of Ceremonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chuping rose to master of ceremonial affairs.

sentences.zh: 處平子璹、珽，別有傳。

translations.literal: Chuping's sons Yu and Ting have separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Chuping's sons Yu and Ting are treated in separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 顏籀，字師古，雍州萬年人，齊黃門侍郎之推孫也。

translations.literal: Yan Zhou, style name Shigu, was a man of Wannian in Yongzhou and grandson of Yan Zhitui, Vice Director of the Yellow Gate of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shigu, whose formal name was Zhou, came from Wannian in Yongzhou and was the grandson of the Qi vice director of the yellow gate, Yan Zhitui.

sentences.zh: 其先本居琅邪，世仕江左。

translations.literal: His ancestors originally dwelt in Langya and for generations served in the lands south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: His family originally came from Langya and for generations served south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 及之推，歷事周、齊，齊滅，始居關中。

translations.literal: By the time of Zhitui he had served Zhou and Qi; when Qi fell, the family first settled in the Guanzhong region.
translations.idiomatic: By Zhitui's time the family had served Zhou and Qi; after Qi's fall they settled in Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 父思魯，以學藝稱，武德初為秦王府記室參軍。

translations.literal: His father Silu was famed for learning and the arts; at the beginning of Wude he was Recorder-Adjutant of the Prince of Qin's household.
translations.idiomatic: His father Silu was known for scholarship and the arts and early in Wude served as recorder-adjutant in the Prince of Qin's household.

sentences.zh: 師古少傳家業，博覽群書，尤精詁訓，善屬文。

translations.literal: Shigu in youth transmitted the family profession, broadly read the many books, was especially skilled in glossarial exegesis, and was good at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu inherited the family scholarly tradition in youth, read widely, excelled in philological commentary, and wrote with skill.

sentences.zh: 隋仁壽中，為尚書左丞李綱所薦，授安養尉。

translations.literal: During the Renshou era of the Sui he was recommended by Li Gang, Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs, and appointed Magistrate of Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sui Renshou era he was recommended by Li Gang, left assistant of the department of state affairs, and appointed magistrate of Anyang.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射楊素見師古年弱貌羸，因謂曰：「安養劇縣，何以克當？」

translations.literal: Yang Su, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, saw that Shigu was young in years and frail in appearance and therefore said to him: "Anyang is a demanding county—how can you be equal to it?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su, left vice director of the department of state affairs, saw how young and slight Shigu looked and asked, "Anyang is a difficult county—how can you manage it?"

sentences.zh: 師古曰：「割雞焉用牛刀。」

translations.literal: Shigu said: "To slaughter a chicken, why use an ox-knife?"
translations.idiomatic: Shigu replied, "To slaughter a chicken, why use an ox-knife?"

sentences.zh: 素奇其對。

translations.literal: Su marveled at his reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su was struck by his answer.

sentences.zh: 到官果以干理聞。

translations.literal: On reaching his post he was indeed famed for capable administration.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he proved himself an able administrator.

sentences.zh: 時薛道衡為襄州總管，與高祖有舊，又悅其才，有所綴文，嘗使其掎摭疵病，甚親暱之。

translations.literal: At that time Xue Daoheng was Regional Commander of Xiangzhou; he had old ties with Gaozu and also delighted in Shigu's talent; whenever he had literary pieces he would have Shigu pick out flaws and faults, and was very intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Daoheng, then regional commander of Xiangzhou, was an old acquaintance of Gaozu and admired Shigu's talent; he often had Shigu critique his drafts and grew very close to him.

sentences.zh: 尋坐事免，歸長安，十年不得調，家貧，以教授為業。

translations.literal: Soon he was dismissed for an offense, returned to Chang'an, and for ten years received no appointment; his household was poor and he made his living by teaching.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon dismissed for an offense, returned to Chang'an, and went ten years without a post; poor at home, he supported himself by teaching.

sentences.zh: 及起義，師古至長春宮謁見，授朝散大夫。

translations.literal: When the uprising began, Shigu went to the Everlasting Spring Palace to pay his respects and was appointed Grand Master for Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion began, Shigu presented himself at the Everlasting Spring Palace and was made grand master for palace counsel.

sentences.zh: 從平京城，拜敦煌公府文學，轉起居舍人，再遷中書舍人，專掌機密。

translations.literal: He followed in the pacification of the capital, was appointed Literary Scholar of the Duke of Dunhuang's household, transferred to Diarist, and again transferred to Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat, exclusively managing confidential matters.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in capturing the capital, became literary scholar in the Duke of Dunhuang's household, then diarist, and was twice promoted until he became drafting attendant of the Secretariat in charge of confidential documents.

sentences.zh: 於時軍國多務，凡有制誥，皆成其手。

translations.literal: At that time military and state affairs were many; whatever edicts and decrees there were all came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: With military and civil affairs pressing on every side, nearly every edict and decree passed through his hand.

sentences.zh: 師古達於政理，冊奏之工，時無及者。

translations.literal: Shigu was accomplished in governmental principles and skilled in memorials and documents; none of the time could equal him.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu understood governance and excelled at formal memorials; none of his contemporaries could match him.

sentences.zh: 太宗踐祚，擢拜中書侍郎，封琅邪縣男。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne he was promoted and appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Baron of Langya County.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong ascended the throne he was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as baron of Langya County.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office upon mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，復為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he again became Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he returned as vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，坐事免。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 太宗以經籍去聖久遠，文字訛謬，令師古於秘書省考定《五經》，師古多所釐正，既成，奏之。

translations.literal: Because the classics had been distant from the sages for long and the written characters were erroneous, Taizong ordered Shigu at the Secretariat to examine and fix the Five Classics; Shigu made many corrections, and when finished presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Because the classics had long been corrupted in transmission, Taizong had Shigu collate the Five Classics at the imperial library; Shigu corrected many errors and presented the finished text.

sentences.zh: 太宗復遣諸儒重加詳議，於時諸儒傳習已久，皆共非之。

translations.literal: Taizong again sent the various Confucians to deliberate in detail; at that time the Confucians had long transmitted and studied the old versions and all together criticized him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong then had other scholars review the work, but they had studied the old texts for generations and united in criticizing him.

sentences.zh: 師古輒引晉、宋已來古今本，隨言曉答，援據詳明，皆出其意表，諸儒莫不歎服。

translations.literal: Shigu would cite ancient and modern texts from Jin and Song onward, answering on the spot with clear explanation; his citations were detailed and explicit, all beyond their expectations, and the Confucians none failed to sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu cited ancient and modern texts from Jin and Song onward, answered every objection on the spot with precise evidence, and left the scholars speechless with admiration.

sentences.zh: 於是兼通直郎、散騎常侍，頒其所定之書於天下，令學者習焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was concurrently made Direct Gentleman and Regular Attendant, and the books he had fixed were promulgated throughout the realm for scholars to study.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made direct gentleman and regular attendant, and his collated classics were issued empire-wide for students to follow.

sentences.zh: 貞觀七年，拜秘書少監，專典刊正。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenguan he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and exclusively supervised collation and correction.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 7 he became vice director of the imperial library with sole charge of textual collation.

sentences.zh: 所有奇書難字，眾所共惑者，隨疑剖析，曲盡其源。

translations.literal: Whatever rare books and difficult characters there were that puzzled everyone, he would analyze each doubt and exhaust the sources in every turn.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever rare texts or difficult characters baffled others, he analyzed the problem and traced it to its source.

sentences.zh: 是時多引後進之士為讎校，師古抑素流，先貴勢，雖富商大賈亦引進之，物論稱其納賄，由是出為郴州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time many junior scholars were brought in for collation; Shigu suppressed plain commoners and favored the noble and powerful—even great merchant magnates he brought in; public opinion said he accepted bribes, and for this he was sent out as Governor of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Though many junior scholars were brought in to help collate texts, Shigu favored the well-connected over humble talent—even wealthy merchants—and was widely accused of taking bribes; for this he was sent out as governor of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 未行，太宗惜其才，謂之曰「卿之學識，良有可稱，但事親居官，未為清論所許。

translations.literal: Before he departed, Taizong regretted his talent and said to him: "Your learning and knowledge are truly worthy of praise, but in serving kin and holding office you have not won approval from pure opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Before he left, Taizong, reluctant to lose him, said, "Your learning is truly admirable, but your conduct toward kin and in office has not won the approval of respectable opinion.

sentences.zh: 今之此授，卿自取之。

translations.literal: This present appointment you have brought on yourself.
translations.idiomatic: This appointment you have brought on yourself.

sentences.zh: 朕以卿曩日任使，不忍遐棄，宜深自誡勵也。」

translations.literal: Because of your former service I cannot bear to cast you far away; you should deeply admonish and encourage yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Because of your past service I cannot bear to cast you aside; you must discipline yourself more strictly."

sentences.zh: 於是復以為秘書少監。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was again made Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was then restored as vice director of the imperial library.

sentences.zh: 師古既負其才，又早見驅策，累被任用，及頻有罪譴，意甚喪沮。

translations.literal: Shigu, having relied on his talent and having early been driven to service, was repeatedly appointed; when he was frequently punished and reprimanded, his spirit was greatly cast down.
translations.idiomatic: Proud of his talent and long accustomed to high office, Shigu grew deeply dejected after repeated censures.

sentences.zh: 自是闔門守靜，杜絕賓客，放志園亭，葛巾野服。

translations.literal: From then on he kept his household in quiet, cut off guests, let his will roam in gardens and pavilions, and wore hemp headcloth and rustic dress.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he kept to his household in seclusion, refused visitors, and wandered his gardens in rustic dress.

sentences.zh: 然搜求古蹟及古器，耽好不已。

translations.literal: Yet he searched for ancient traces and ancient vessels and indulged his love without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he never ceased searching out antiquities and ancient artifacts.

sentences.zh: 俄又奉詔與博士等撰定《五禮》，十一年，《禮》成，進爵為子。

translations.literal: Soon he again received an edict to compile, together with the erudites and others, the Five Rites; in the eleventh year the Rites were completed and his rank was advanced to Viscount.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to help the erudites compile the Five Rites; when the work was finished in the eleventh year he was raised to viscount.

sentences.zh: 時承乾在東宮，命師古注班固《漢書》，解釋詳明，深為學者所重。

translations.literal: At that time Chengan was in the Eastern Palace and ordered Shigu to annotate Ban Gu's Book of Han; the explanations were detailed and clear and were deeply valued by scholars.
translations.idiomatic: While Chengan was crown prince he had Shigu annotate Ban Gu's Book of Han; the commentary was detailed and clear and won great esteem among scholars.

sentences.zh: 承乾表上之，太宗令編之秘閣，賜師古物二百段、良馬一匹。

translations.literal: Chengan submitted it in a memorial; Taizong ordered it compiled in the Secret Archive and bestowed on Shigu two hundred bolts of goods and one fine horse.
translations.idiomatic: Chengan presented it to the throne; Taizong had it stored in the imperial archive and rewarded Shigu with two hundred bolts of goods and a fine horse.

sentences.zh: 十五年，太宗下詔，將有事於泰山，所司與公卿並諸儒博士詳定儀注。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Emperor Taizong issued an edict, intending to perform the fengshan rite at Mount Tai; the relevant offices together with the high ministers and various Confucian erudites and academicians were to discuss and fix the ritual protocols in detail.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, Emperor Taizong issued an edict announcing his intention to perform the fengshan sacrifice at Mount Tai, and ordered the responsible offices, together with the chief ministers and all Confucian scholars and academicians, to work out the ritual protocols in detail.

sentences.zh: 太常卿韋挺、禮部侍郎令狐德棻為封禪使，參考其儀，時論者競起異端。

translations.literal: Chief Minister of Ceremonials Wei Ting and Vice Minister of Rites Linghu Defen were appointed commissioners for the fengshan rite to consult its rituals; at the time commentators all raised divergent views.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ting, Chief Minister of Ceremonials, and Linghu Defen, Vice Minister of Rites, were appointed commissioners for the fengshan rite to study its ceremonies, but at the time commentators all raised conflicting opinions.

sentences.zh: 師古奏曰：「臣撰定《封禪儀注書》在十一年春，於時諸儒參詳，以為適中。」

translations.literal: Shigu memorialized, saying: "Your subject drafted and finalized the Book of Fengshan Ritual Protocols in the spring of the eleventh year; at that time various Confucians examined it together and considered it appropriately balanced."
translations.idiomatic: Shigu submitted a memorial, saying, "Your subject completed the Book of Fengshan Ritual Protocols in the spring of the eleventh year; at that time the Confucian scholars reviewed it together and judged it to strike the right balance."

sentences.zh: 於是詔公卿定其可否，多從師古之說，然而事竟不行。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered the high ministers to determine its feasibility; most followed Shigu's view, yet in the end the matter was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered the chief ministers to decide whether it was feasible; most sided with Shigu's proposal, but in the end the project was never carried out.

sentences.zh: 師古俄遷秘書監、弘文館學士。

translations.literal: Shigu was soon transferred to Director of the Palace Library and Academician of the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu was soon promoted to Director of the Palace Library and appointed an Academician of the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 十九年，從駕東巡，道病卒，年六十五，謚曰戴。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, he accompanied the imperial tour eastward, fell ill on the road, and died, aged sixty-five; his posthumous title was Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, while accompanying the emperor on an eastern tour, he fell ill on the road and died at the age of sixty-five; his posthumous title was Dai.

sentences.zh: 有集六十捲。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in sixty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in sixty juan.

sentences.zh: 其所注《漢書》及《急就章》，大行於世。

translations.literal: His commentaries on the Book of Han and the Rapid Writing Primer circulated widely in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His commentaries on the Book of Han and the Rapid Writing Primer became widely circulated.

sentences.zh: 永徽三年，師古子揚庭為符璽郎，又表上師古所撰《匡謬正俗》八卷。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yonghui, Shigu's son Yangting served as Director of Seals and Credentials, and again memorialized presenting Shigu's eight juan Correcting Errors and Rectifying Custom.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yonghui, Shigu's son Yangting, who was serving as Director of Seals and Credentials, again submitted a memorial presenting his father's eight-juan work Correcting Errors and Rectifying Custom.

sentences.zh: 高宗下詔付秘書閣，仍賜揚庭帛五十匹。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong issued an edict to deposit it in the Secretariat archives, and also granted Yangting fifty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong issued an edict ordering the work deposited in the Secretariat archives and also granted Yangting fifty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 師古弟相時，亦有學業。

translations.literal: Shigu's younger brother Xiangshi also had scholarly accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu's younger brother Xiangshi was also a man of learning.

sentences.zh: 武德中，與房玄齡等為秦府學士。

translations.literal: During the Wude era, together with Fang Xuanling and others he served as an academician in the Prince of Qin's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wude era, he served alongside Fang Xuanling and others as an academician in the Prince of Qin's household.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，累遷諫議大夫，拾遺補闕，有諍臣之風。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era, he was repeatedly promoted to Remonstrance and Censor, remedying oversights and filling gaps, with the bearing of a loyal critic.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era, he rose through repeated promotions to Remonstrance and Censor, correcting oversights and filling gaps in policy, with the bearing of a loyal critic.

sentences.zh: 尋轉禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 相時羸瘠多疾病，太宗常使賜以醫藥。

translations.literal: Xiangshi was emaciated and often ill; Emperor Taizong frequently had medicines sent to him as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangshi was frail and frequently ill, and Emperor Taizong often sent him medicines as gifts.

sentences.zh: 性仁友，及師古卒，不勝哀慕而卒。

translations.literal: By nature he was benevolent and friendly; when Shigu died, he could not bear the grief and mourning, and died as well.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was kind and affectionate; when Shigu died, he was overcome with grief and mourning and died as well.

sentences.zh: 師古叔父游秦，武德初累遷廉州刺史，封臨沂縣男。

translations.literal: Shigu's uncle Youqin, at the beginning of Wude was repeatedly promoted to Prefect of Lianzhou, ennobled as Marquis of Linyi County.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu's uncle Youqin, at the beginning of the Wude era, rose through repeated promotions to Prefect of Lianzhou and was ennobled as Marquis of Linyi County.

sentences.zh: 時劉黑闥初平，人多以強暴寡禮，風俗未安，游秦撫卹境內，敬讓大行。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Heita had just been pacified; many people were violent and lacking in ritual propriety, and local customs were not yet settled; Youqin comforted and soothed the territory, and reverence and yielding became widely practiced.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Liu Heita had just been pacified; many people were violent and disrespectful, and local customs had not yet settled. Youqin comforted and cared for the people within his jurisdiction, and courtesy and forbearance became widely practiced.

sentences.zh: 邑裡歌曰：「廉州顏有道，性行同莊、老。

translations.literal: A district song said: "Prefect Yan of Lianzhou has the Way; his nature and conduct are like Zhuangzi and Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: A local song ran: "Prefect Yan of Lianzhou possesses the Way; in nature and conduct he is like Zhuangzi and Laozi.

sentences.zh: 愛人如赤子，不殺非時草。」

translations.literal: He loves people as infants and does not cut grasses out of season."
translations.idiomatic: He loves the people as his own children and will not cut grass out of season."

sentences.zh: 高祖璽書勞勉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu sent an imperial letter of commendation and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu sent an imperial letter commending and encouraging him.

sentences.zh: 俄拜鄆州刺史，卒於官。

translations.literal: He was soon appointed Prefect of Yanzhou and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Prefect of Yanzhou and died in office.

sentences.zh: 撰《漢書決疑》十二卷，為學者所稱，後師古注《漢書》，亦多取其義耳。

translations.literal: He composed Clarifying Doubts on the Book of Han in twelve juan, praised by scholars; later when Shigu annotated the Book of Han, he also drew much from its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Clarifying Doubts on the Book of Han in twelve juan, which scholars praised; later, when Shigu annotated the Book of Han, he drew heavily on its interpretations as well.

sentences.zh: 令狐德棻，宜州華原人，隋鴻臚少卿熙之子也。

translations.literal: Linghu Defen was a native of Huayuan in Yizhou; he was the son of Xi, former Vice Director of the Directorate for Guests of the Sui dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Defen was a native of Huayuan in Yizhou and the son of Xi, who had served as Vice Director of the Directorate for Guests under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 先居燉煌，代為河西右族。

translations.literal: His ancestors originally lived in Dunhuang and for generations were a great clan on the right bank of the Hexi region.
translations.idiomatic: His family had originally lived in Dunhuang and for generations had been a leading clan of the Hexi region.

sentences.zh: 德棻博涉文史，早知名。

translations.literal: Defen was broadly versed in literature and history and achieved renown early.
translations.idiomatic: Defen was widely versed in literature and history and won early renown.

sentences.zh: 大業末，為藥城長，以世亂不就職。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era, he was appointed Magistrate of Yaocheng but, because of the chaos of the age, did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye era, he was appointed magistrate of Yaocheng, but because of the turmoil of the times he never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 及義旗建，淮安王神通據太平宮，自稱總管，以德棻為記室參軍。

translations.literal: When the righteous banner was raised, Prince Huai'an Li Shentong seized the Taiping Palace and styled himself Commander-in-Chief, appointing Defen as Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous banner was raised, Prince Huai'an Li Shentong seized the Taiping Palace, styled himself Commander-in-Chief, and appointed Defen as his secretariat attendant.

sentences.zh: 高祖入關，引直大丞相府記室。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu entered the passes, he summoned him to serve as Recorder in the Grand Chancellor's direct office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu entered the passes, he summoned Defen to serve as a recorder in the Grand Chancellor's direct office.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，轉起居舍人，甚見親待。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude, he was transferred to Diarist of the Emperor's Actions, and received great intimacy and favor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude, he was appointed Diarist of the Emperor's Actions and enjoyed great intimacy and favor.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷秘書丞，與侍中陳叔達等受詔撰《藝文類聚》。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was promoted to Secretary Director and, together with Vice Director Chen Shuda and others, received an edict to compile the Literary Categories Collection.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, he was promoted to Secretary Director and, together with Vice Director Chen Shuda and others, received an edict to compile the Literary Categories Collection.

sentences.zh: 高祖問德棻曰：「比者，丈夫冠、婦人髻，競為高大，何也？」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu asked Defen: "Of late, men's caps and women's coiffures all compete to be tall and large—why is this?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu asked Defen, "Recently, men's caps and women's hairstyles have all been competing to grow taller and larger—why is that?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「在人之身，冠為上飾，所以古人方諸君上。

translations.literal: He replied: "On the human body the cap is the foremost ornament; that is why the ancients likened it to the ruler above.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "On the human body, the cap is the highest adornment; that is why the ancients compared it to the ruler above.

sentences.zh: 昔東晉之末，君弱臣強，江左士女，皆衣小而裳大。

translations.literal: In the last years of the Eastern Jin, the ruler was weak and ministers strong; scholars and women south of the Yangzi all wore small jackets and large skirts.
