translations.idiomatic: In the final years of the Eastern Jin, the ruler was weak and his ministers strong; scholars and women south of the Yangzi all wore short jackets and long skirts.

sentences.zh: 及宋武正位之後，君德尊嚴，衣服之制，俄亦變改。

translations.literal: After Emperor Wu of Song took the throne, the ruler's virtue became solemn and great, and the system of dress soon changed as well.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Song ascended the throne, the ruler's authority became solemn and imposing, and the style of dress soon changed as well.

sentences.zh: 此即近事之征。」

translations.literal: This is evidence from recent events."
translations.idiomatic: This is proof drawn from recent events."

sentences.zh: 高祖然之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu approved.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu agreed with him.

sentences.zh: 時承喪亂之餘，經籍亡逸，德棻奏請購募遺書。

translations.literal: At the time, in the aftermath of war and disorder, the classics had been lost and scattered; Defen memorialized requesting that missing books be purchased and sought.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, in the aftermath of war and chaos, many classics had been lost; Defen submitted a memorial requesting that missing books be purchased and collected.

sentences.zh: 重加錢帛，增置楷書，令繕寫。

translations.literal: He added funds in silver and cloth and increased the number of clerks assigned to regular script, ordering them to copy them out.
translations.idiomatic: Additional money and silk were offered, more copyists were assigned, and orders were given to transcribe the texts.

sentences.zh: 數年間，群書略備。

translations.literal: Within a few years, the books were largely complete.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years, the collection of books was largely complete.

sentences.zh: 德棻嘗從容言於高祖曰：「竊見近代已來，多無正史，梁、陳及齊，猶有文籍。

translations.literal: Defen once said calmly to Emperor Gaozu: "I have observed that in recent times many dynasties lack proper official histories; Liang, Chen, and Qi still have literary records.
translations.idiomatic: Defen once said calmly to Emperor Gaozu, "I have noticed that in recent times many dynasties lack proper official histories; the Liang, Chen, and Qi still have written records.

sentences.zh: 至周、隋遭大業離亂，多有遺闕。

translations.literal: As for Zhou and Sui, they suffered the disorder of the Great Enterprise era, and many records are missing.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Zhou and Sui, they suffered the chaos of the Daye era, and many records have been lost.

sentences.zh: 當今耳目猶接，尚有可憑，如更十數年後，恐事蹟湮沒。

translations.literal: At present our ears and eyes still reach back, and there are still sources to rely on; but after another ten-odd years, I fear the events will be lost and forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: At present we can still hear and see what happened, and there are still sources to rely on; but after another ten years or so, I fear those events will be lost forever.

sentences.zh: 陛上既受禪於隋，復承周氏曆數，國家二祖功業，並在周時。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, having received the abdication from Sui, also inherited the Zhou dynastic mandate; both founding ancestors' achievements lay in the Zhou period.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty received the abdication from the Sui and also inherited the Zhou dynastic line; the achievements of our state's two founding ancestors both belong to the Zhou period.

sentences.zh: 如文史不存，何以貽鑑今古？

translations.literal: If literature and history are not preserved, how can they be bequeathed as mirrors for past and present?
translations.idiomatic: If these writings and historical records are not preserved, how can they be handed down as mirrors for past and present?

sentences.zh: 如臣愚見，並請修之。」

translations.literal: In this humble subject's view, I request that all be compiled."
translations.idiomatic: In this humble subject's view, I ask that they all be compiled."

sentences.zh: 高祖然其奏，下詔曰：

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu approved the memorial and issued an edict saying:
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu approved the memorial and issued an edict, saying:

sentences.zh: 司典序言，史官記事，考論得失，究盡變通。

translations.literal: Those who preside over canonical precedents and set forth the preface, and the historiographers who record events, examine and discuss gains and losses and exhaustively investigate change and adaptation—
translations.idiomatic: Those who oversee canonical texts and set forth prefaces, and the historiographers who record events, examine gains and losses and exhaustively investigate change and adaptation—

sentences.zh: 所以裁成義類，懲惡勸善，多識前古，貽鑑將來。

translations.literal: by this they shape righteous categories, punish evil and encourage good, gain broad knowledge of antiquity, and leave mirrors for the future.
translations.idiomatic: by this they shape moral categories, punish evil and encourage good, broaden knowledge of antiquity, and leave mirrors for generations to come.

sentences.zh: 伏羲以降，周、秦斯及，兩漢傳緒，三國受命，迄於晉、宋，載籍備焉。

translations.literal: From Fuxi downward through Zhou and Qin, on to the two Han dynasties' transmission of the line, the Three Kingdoms' reception of the mandate, down to Jin and Song—the records are complete.
translations.idiomatic: From Fuxi down through Zhou and Qin, through the succession of the two Han dynasties, the Three Kingdoms' receipt of the mandate, and down to Jin and Song—the historical records are complete.

sentences.zh: 自有魏南徙，乘機撫運，周、隋禪代，歷世相仍。

translations.literal: From when Wei moved south, it seized the opportunity and governed the age; Zhou and Sui succeeded by abdication through generations continuous.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Wei moved south and seized the opportunity to rule the age, through Zhou and Sui, which succeeded by abdication across successive generations—

sentences.zh: 梁氏稱邦，跨據淮海；

translations.literal: Liang established a state spanning the Huai and the sea;
translations.idiomatic: Liang established a realm spanning the Huai River and the sea;

sentences.zh: 齊遷龜鼎，陳建皇宗，莫不自命正朔，綿歷歲祀，各殊徽號，刪定禮儀。

translations.literal: Qi moved the imperial tripod; Chen founded an imperial house—each on their own claimed the correct calendar, lasted through years and generations, each had its distinct standard and reign title, and revised and fixed ritual and etiquette.
translations.idiomatic: Qi moved the imperial tripod, and Chen founded an imperial house—each in turn claimed the correct calendar, endured through years and generations, adopted its own reign titles and standards, and revised and fixed ritual and etiquette.

sentences.zh: 至於發跡開基，受終告代，嘉謀善政，名臣奇士，立言著績，無乏於時。

translations.literal: As for the unfolding of enterprise and founding of dynastic bases, the conclusion of rule and announcement of succession, wise counsels and good policies, famous ministers and extraordinary worthies, establishing words and displaying achievements—all were abundant in their times.
translations.idiomatic: As for the founding of dynasties, the transfer of rule and announcement of succession, wise counsels and good policies, famous ministers and extraordinary men of talent, and those who left words and achievements on record—all were abundant in their times.

sentences.zh: 然而簡牘未編，紀傳咸闕，炎涼已積，謠俗遷訛。

translations.literal: Yet the bamboo slips were not compiled, annals and biographies were all wanting, cold and heat had piled up over time, and customs and lore had shifted into error.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the bamboo slips were never compiled, annals and biographies remain incomplete, years have piled up like alternating cold and heat, and popular lore has drifted into error.

sentences.zh: 餘烈遺風，倏焉將墜。

translations.literal: The remaining glory and surviving ways would in a flash nearly fall.
translations.idiomatic: Their remaining glory and surviving customs would in an instant nearly vanish.

sentences.zh: 朕握圖馭宇，長世字人，方立典謨，永垂憲則。

translations.literal: I hold the chart and govern the realm, long to sustain and cherish my people, and am just now establishing institutions and canons, to be handed down forever as fundamental law.
translations.idiomatic: I hold the imperial chart and govern the realm, long to sustain and nurture my people, and am now establishing institutions and canons to be handed down forever as fundamental law.

sentences.zh: 顧彼湮落，用深軫悼，有懷撰次，實資良直。

translations.literal: Looking at those perished and fallen records, my grief is deeply pained; with intent to compile and order them, I truly rely on the good and upright.
translations.idiomatic: When I look upon those records lost and fallen into ruin, my grief is deep; in my desire to compile and order them, I truly rely on men of integrity and talent.

sentences.zh: 中書令蕭瑀、給事中王敬業、著作郎殷聞禮可修魏史，侍中陳叔達、秘書丞令狐德棻、太史令庾儉可修周史，兼中書令封德彝、中書舍人顏師古可修隋史，大理卿崔善為、中書舍人孔紹安、太子洗馬蕭德言可修梁史，太子詹事裴矩、兼吏部郎中祖孝孫、前秘書丞魏徵可修齊史，秘書監竇璡、給事中歐陽詢、秦王文學姚思廉可修陳史。

translations.literal: Central Secretariat Director Xiao Yu, Palace Attendant Wang Jingye, and Compilation Officer Yin Wenli are authorized to compile the Wei history; Vice Director Chen Shuda, Secretary Director Linghu Defen, and Director of the Imperial Astronomical Bureau Yu Jian are authorized to compile the Zhou history; concurrently Central Secretariat Director Feng Deyi and Drafting Secretariat Attendant Yan Shigu are authorized to compile the Sui history; Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Cui Shanwei, Drafting Secretariat Attendant Kong Shao'an, and Palace Groom of the Heir Apparent Xiao Deyan are authorized to compile the Liang history; Grand Steward of the Heir Apparent Pei Ju, concurrently Director in the Ministry of Personnel Zu Xiaosun, and former Secretary Director Wei Zheng are authorized to compile the Qi history; Director of the Palace Library Dou Jin, Palace Attendant Ouyang Xun, and Literary Instructor to the Prince of Qin Yao Silian are authorized to compile the Chen history.
translations.idiomatic: Central Secretariat Director Xiao Yu, Palace Attendant Wang Jingye, and Compilation Officer Yin Wenli shall compile the history of Wei; Vice Director Chen Shuda, Secretary Director Linghu Defen, and Director of the Imperial Astronomical Bureau Yu Jian shall compile the history of Zhou; concurrently serving Central Secretariat Director Feng Deyi and Drafting Secretariat Attendant Yan Shigu shall compile the history of Sui; Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Cui Shanwei, Drafting Secretariat Attendant Kong Shao'an, and Palace Groom of the Heir Apparent Xiao Deyan shall compile the history of Liang; Grand Steward of the Heir Apparent Pei Ju, concurrently serving Director in the Ministry of Personnel Zu Xiaosun, and former Secretary Director Wei Zheng shall compile the history of Qi; Director of the Palace Library Dou Jin, Palace Attendant Ouyang Xun, and Literary Instructor to the Prince of Qin Yao Silian shall compile the history of Chen.

sentences.zh: 務加詳核，博采舊聞，義在不刊，書法無隱。

translations.literal: Make every effort to examine and verify thoroughly, broadly gather old reports; righteousness requires that what is written cannot be altered, and the historiographic method admits no concealment.
translations.idiomatic: They shall examine and verify everything with the greatest care, broadly gather earlier accounts, write with integrity so that what is recorded cannot be altered, and follow historiographic principles that admit no concealment.

sentences.zh: 瑀等受詔，曆數年，竟不能就而罷。

translations.literal: Yu and the others received the edict; over several years they ultimately could not complete it and the project was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and the others received the edict, but after several years they still could not finish the work, and the project was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，太宗復敕修撰，乃令德棻與秘書郎岑文本修周史，中書舍人李百藥修齊史，著作郎姚思廉修梁、陳史，秘書監魏徵修隋史，與尚書左僕射房玄齡總監諸代史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan, Emperor Taizong again ordered the compilation; he then appointed Defen together with Secretary Gentleman Cen Wenben to compile the Zhou history, Drafting Secretariat Attendant Li Baiyao to compile the Qi history, Compilation Officer Yao Silian to compile the Liang and Chen histories, Director of the Palace Library Wei Zheng to compile the Sui history, and together with Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Fang Xuanling to oversee all the dynastic histories.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenguan, Emperor Taizong again ordered the histories compiled. He appointed Defen and Secretary Gentleman Cen Wenben to compile the Zhou history, Drafting Secretariat Attendant Li Baiyao to compile the Qi history, Compilation Officer Yao Silian to compile the Liang and Chen histories, and Director of the Palace Library Wei Zheng to compile the Sui history, with Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Fang Xuanling overseeing all the dynastic histories.

sentences.zh: 眾議以魏史既有魏收、魏彥二家，已為詳備，遂不復修。

translations.literal: In collective discussion it was held that the Wei history already had the two works of Wei Shou and Wei Yan and was already detailed and complete, so they did not compile it again.
translations.idiomatic: In discussion the court held that the history of Wei already existed in the detailed works of Wei Shou and Wei Yan, so no new compilation of the Wei history was undertaken.

sentences.zh: 德棻又奏引殿中侍御史崔仁師佐修周史，德棻仍總知類會梁、陳、齊、隋諸史。

translations.literal: Defen again memorialized recommending Palace Attendant Cui Renshi to assist in compiling the Zhou history; Defen still overall supervised the classification and collation of the Liang, Chen, Qi, and Sui histories.
translations.idiomatic: Defen submitted another memorial recommending Palace Attendant Cui Renshi to assist in compiling the Zhou history, while Defen himself continued to oversee the classification and collation of the Liang, Chen, Qi, and Sui histories.

sentences.zh: 武德已來創修撰之源，自德棻始也。

translations.literal: The source of the compilation projects initiated since Wude began with Defen.
translations.idiomatic: The origin of the historiographical projects begun since the Wude era lay with Defen.

sentences.zh: 六年，累遷禮部侍郎，兼修國史，賜爵彭陽男。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Rites, concurrently compiling the national history, and ennobled as Baron of Pengyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, he rose through repeated promotions to Vice Minister of Rites, was concurrently charged with compiling the national history, and was ennobled as Baron of Pengyang.

sentences.zh: 十年，以修周史賜絹四百匹。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, for compiling the Zhou history he was granted four hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, he was granted four hundred bolts of silk for his work on the Zhou history.

sentences.zh: 十一年，修《新禮》成，進爵為子。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when the compilation of the New Rites was completed, he was promoted in rank to Viscount.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, when the New Rites was completed, his noble rank was raised to viscount.

sentences.zh: 又以撰《氏族志》成，賜帛二百匹。

translations.literal: Again, for completing the compilation of the Genealogical Records of Clans, he was granted two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was also granted two hundred bolts of silk for completing the Genealogical Records of Clans.

sentences.zh: 十五年，轉太子右庶子。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 承乾敗，隨例除名。

translations.literal: When Chengqian fell, he was removed from office according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengqian's plot failed, Defen was dismissed from office according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 十八年，起為雅州刺史，以公事免。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he was recalled and appointed Prefect of Yazhou, but was dismissed for an official matter.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, he was recalled and appointed Prefect of Yazhou, but was later dismissed over an official matter.

sentences.zh: 尋有詔改撰《晉書》，房玄齡奏德棻令預修撰，當時同修一十八人，並推德棻為首，其體制多取決焉。

translations.literal: Soon an edict was issued to revise and compile the Book of Jin; Fang Xuanling memorialized that Defen should take part in the compilation; at the time there were eighteen co-compilers in all, and all regarded Defen as the leader; its format and structure were largely decided by him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward an edict ordered a revised compilation of the Book of Jin; Fang Xuanling memorialized that Defen should take part in the project. At the time there were eighteen co-compilers in all, and all regarded Defen as their leader; the work's format and structure were largely decided by him.

sentences.zh: 書成，除秘書少監。

translations.literal: When the book was completed, he was appointed Vice Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: When the book was completed, he was appointed Vice Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年，又受詔撰定律令，復為禮部侍郎，兼弘文館學士，監修國史及《五代史志》。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghui, he again received an edict to compile laws and ordinances, was again appointed Vice Minister of Rites, concurrently an Academician of the Hongwen Institute, and supervised the compilation of the national history and the Treatises of the Five Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yonghui, he again received an edict to help compile laws and ordinances, was reappointed Vice Minister of Rites and Academician of the Hongwen Institute, and was charged with supervising the national history and the Treatises of the Five Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 尋遷太常卿，兼弘文館學士。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to Chief Minister of Ceremonials, concurrently an Academician of the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Chief Minister of Ceremonials while continuing to serve as an Academician of the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 時高宗初嗣位，留心政道，嘗召宰臣及弘文館學士於中華殿而問曰：「何者為王道；

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Gaozong had just succeeded to the throne and was attentive to the way of governance; he once summoned the chief ministers and the Hongwen Institute academicians to the Zhonghua Hall and asked: "What is the kingly way;
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Gaozong had just ascended the throne and was attentive to the way of governance; he once summoned the chief ministers and the Hongwen Institute academicians to the Zhonghua Hall and asked, "What is the kingly way,

sentences.zh: 霸道？

translations.literal: and what is the hegemonic way?
translations.idiomatic: and what is the hegemonic way?

sentences.zh: 又孰為先後？」

translations.literal: And which comes first and which comes after?"
translations.idiomatic: And which should come first, and which after?"

sentences.zh: 德棻對曰：「王道任德，霸道任刑。

translations.literal: Defen replied: "The kingly way relies on virtue; the hegemonic way relies on punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Defen replied, "The kingly way relies on virtue; the hegemonic way relies on punishment.

sentences.zh: 自三王已上，皆行王道；

translations.literal: From the Three Sage-Kings upward, all practiced the kingly way;
translations.idiomatic: From the Three Sage-Kings onward, all practiced the kingly way;

sentences.zh: 唯秦任霸術，漢則雜而行之；

translations.literal: only Qin employed hegemonic methods, while Han mixed the two in practice;
translations.idiomatic: only Qin employed hegemonic methods, while Han mixed the two in practice;

sentences.zh: 魏、晉已下，王、霸俱失。

translations.literal: from Wei and Jin downward, both the kingly and hegemonic ways were lost.
translations.idiomatic: from Wei and Jin downward, both the kingly and hegemonic ways were lost.

sentences.zh: 如欲用之，王道為最，而行之為難。」

translations.literal: If one wishes to employ them, the kingly way is supreme, yet it is the hardest to practice."
translations.idiomatic: If one wishes to put them into practice, the kingly way is best, but it is also the hardest to carry out."

sentences.zh: 高宗曰：「今之所行，何政為要？」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong said: "Of the policies being practiced now, which is most important?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong said, "Of the policies being pursued now, which is most important?"

sentences.zh: 德棻對曰：「古者為政，清其心，簡其事，以此為本。

translations.literal: Defen replied: "In antiquity in governing, one purified the heart and simplified affairs—this was taken as the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Defen replied, "In antiquity, governing meant purifying the heart and simplifying affairs—that was the foundation.

sentences.zh: 當今天下無虞，年谷豐稔，薄賦斂，少征役，此乃合於古道。

translations.literal: At present the realm is free from alarm, the harvest is abundant, levies are light, and corvée labor is reduced—this accords with the ancient way.
translations.idiomatic: At present the realm is at peace, the harvest is abundant, taxes are light, and corvée labor is reduced—this accords with the ancient way.

sentences.zh: 為政之要道，莫過於此。」

translations.literal: Of the essential points in governing, nothing surpasses this."
translations.idiomatic: Of the essential points of governance, nothing surpasses this."

sentences.zh: 高宗曰：「政道莫尚於無為也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong said: "In the way of governance nothing is greater than non-action."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong said, "In the way of governance, nothing is greater than non-action."

sentences.zh: 又問曰：「禹、湯何以興？

translations.literal: He again asked: "By what did Yu and Tang rise?
translations.idiomatic: He asked again, "By what did Yu and Tang rise?

sentences.zh: 桀、紂何以亡？」

translations.literal: By what did Jie and Zhou perish?"
translations.idiomatic: And by what did Jie and Zhou perish?"

sentences.zh: 德棻對曰：「《傳》稱：『禹、湯罪己，其興也勃焉；

translations.literal: Defen replied: "The Commentary says: 'Yu and Tang blamed themselves, and their rise was swift;
translations.idiomatic: Defen replied, "The Commentary says, 'Yu and Tang blamed themselves, and their rise was swift;

sentences.zh: 桀、紂罪人，其亡也忽焉。』

translations.literal: Jie and Zhou blamed others, and their fall was sudden.'
translations.idiomatic: Jie and Zhou blamed others, and their fall was sudden.'

sentences.zh: 二主惑於妹喜、妲己，誅戮諫者，造砲烙之刑，是其所以亡也。」

translations.literal: The two rulers were deluded by Meixi and Daji, executed those who remonstrated, and created the punishment of the burning pillar—this is why they perished."
translations.idiomatic: Those two rulers were led astray by Meixi and Daji, executed those who remonstrated with them, and invented the burning-pillar punishment—that is why they perished."

sentences.zh: 高宗甚悅，既罷，各賜以繒彩。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong was greatly pleased; when the audience ended, each was granted silk and brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong was greatly pleased; when the audience ended, each participant was granted silk and brocade.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷國子祭酒，以修貞觀十三年以後實錄功，賜物四百段，兼授崇賢館學士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education; for his work compiling the Veritable Records from the thirteenth year of Zhenguan onward, he was granted four hundred items and concurrently appointed an Academician of the Chongxian Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, he was appointed Chancellor of the Directorate of Education; for compiling the Veritable Records from the thirteenth year of Zhenguan onward, he was granted four hundred items and concurrently appointed an Academician of the Chongxian Institute.

sentences.zh: 尋又撰《高宗實錄》三十捲，進爵為公。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he again compiled the Veritable Records of Gaozong in thirty juan and was promoted in noble rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: He soon compiled the Veritable Records of Gaozong in thirty juan and was raised in noble rank to duke.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，表請致仕，許之，仍加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo, he memorialized requesting retirement; permission was granted, and he was additionally appointed Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Longshuo, he submitted a memorial requesting retirement; permission was granted, and he was additionally appointed Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 乾封元年，卒於家，年八十四，謚曰憲。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianfeng, he died at home, aged eighty-four; his posthumous title was Xian.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianfeng, he died at home at the age of eighty-four; his posthumous title was Xian.

sentences.zh: 德棻暮年尤勤於著述，國家凡有修撰，無不參預。

translations.literal: In his old age Defen was especially diligent in writing; of all the state's compilations, there was none in which he did not take part.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Defen was especially diligent in writing, and there was scarcely a state compilation in which he did not take part.

sentences.zh: 自武德已後，有鄧世隆、顧胤、李延壽、李仁實前後修撰國史，頗為當時所稱。

translations.literal: From after Wude onward, there were Deng Shilong, Gu Yin, Li Yanshou, and Li Renshi who successively compiled the national history, and they were quite praised by their contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wude era, Deng Shilong, Gu Yin, Li Yanshou, and Li Renshi compiled the national history in turn, and their work won considerable praise in their day.

sentences.zh: 鄧世隆者，相州人也。

translations.literal: Deng Shilong was a man of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Shilong came from Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 大業末，王世充兄子太，守河陽，引世隆為賓客，大見親遇。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye, Wang Shichong's brother's son Tai held Heyang, brought Shilong in as a guest, and greatly favored and treated him with intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daye reign, Wang Tai—nephew of Wang Shichong—held Heyang and took Shilong on as a retainer, treating him with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 及太宗攻洛陽，遣書諭太，世隆為覆書，言辭不遜。

translations.literal: When the Taizong attacked Luoyang, he sent a letter to instruct Tai; Shilong wrote the reply, and the wording was not deferential.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong besieged Luoyang, he sent Wang Tai a letter of persuasion; Shilong drafted the reply, and its language was defiant.

sentences.zh: 洛陽平後，世隆懼罪，變姓名，自號隱玄先生，竄於白鹿山。

translations.literal: After Luoyang was pacified, Shilong feared punishment, changed his name, styled himself Master Yinuan, and fled to Mount Bailu.
translations.idiomatic: After Luoyang fell, Shilong feared retribution. He changed his name, called himself Master Yinuan, and went into hiding on Mount Bailu.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，征授國子主簿，與崔仁師、慕容善行、劉顗、庾安禮、敬播等俱為修史學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, he was summoned and appointed Director of the National University; together with Cui Renshi, Murong Shanxing, Liu Yi, Yu Anli, Jing Bo, and others, he all served as academicians for compiling history.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenguan years he was summoned to office as Director of the National University and, together with Cui Renshi, Murong Shanxing, Liu Yi, Yu Anli, Jing Bo, and others, appointed an academician charged with compiling history.

sentences.zh: 世隆負宿罪，猶不自安。

translations.literal: Shilong bore an old offense and still did not feel secure.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong still carried the burden of his past offense and could not feel at ease.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞之，遣房玄齡諭之曰：「爾為王太作書，誠合重罪，但各為其主，於朕豈有惡哉？

translations.literal: When the Taizong heard of this, he sent Fang Xuanling to instruct him, saying: "You wrote a letter for Wang Tai — it truly deserved severe punishment, but each serves his own lord — would I bear ill will toward you for that?
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong learned of this, he sent Fang Xuanling to reassure him, saying, "You drafted a letter for Wang Tai — that truly merited heavy punishment, yet each man serves his own master; why should I hold that against you?

sentences.zh: 朕今為天子，何能追責匹夫之過？

translations.literal: Now that I am Son of Heaven, how could I pursue and blame the fault of an ordinary man?
translations.idiomatic: I am Son of Heaven now — how could I still hound an ordinary man's old fault?

sentences.zh: 爾宜坦然，勿懷危懼也。」

translations.literal: You should be at ease and not harbor fear of peril."
translations.idiomatic: Put your mind at rest and do not live in dread."

sentences.zh: 擢授著作佐郎，歷衛尉丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted and appointed Assistant Director of the Bureau of Writings, and served successively as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong was then promoted to Assistant Director of the Bureau of Writings and later served as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗以武功定海內，櫛風沐雨，不暇於詩書。

translations.literal: Initially, the Taizong by martial prowess settled the empire; combing the wind and bathing in the rain, he had no leisure for poetry and books.
translations.idiomatic: At first Taizong had conquered the realm by force of arms, toiling through wind and rain with no time for poetry or the classics.

sentences.zh: 暨於嗣業，進引忠良，銳精思政。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the enterprise, he advanced and brought in the loyal and good, and sharpened his spirit to think on governance.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had inherited the throne, he promoted worthy and loyal men and applied himself keenly to the work of government.

sentences.zh: 數年之後，道致隆平，遂於聽覽之暇，留情文史。

translations.literal: After several years, the Way was attained and peace flourished; then in the leisure of attending to affairs of state, he applied his mind to literature and history.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years good order prevailed and the land prospered, and in the intervals between affairs of state he turned his attention to letters and history.

sentences.zh: 敘事言懷，時有構屬，天才宏麗，興托玄遠。

translations.literal: In narrating events and voicing feelings, he sometimes composed pieces; his natural talent was vast and splendid, and his inspiration reached to the profound and distant.
translations.idiomatic: When he narrated events or gave voice to his thoughts, he sometimes composed literary pieces; his native gift was broad and splendid, and his inspiration ranged into depths far beyond the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十三年，世隆上疏請編錄御集，太宗竟不許之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhenguan, Shilong submitted a memorial requesting compilation of the Imperial Collection; the Taizong ultimately did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 13 Shilong memorialized asking that the emperor's collected writings be edited and preserved, but Taizong refused.

sentences.zh: 世隆又采隋代舊事，撰為《東都記》三十捲。

translations.literal: Shilong also gathered old affairs of the Sui dynasty and compiled them into the Record of the Eastern Capital, thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong also collected materials on the Sui and compiled the Record of the Eastern Capital in thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 遷著作郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be a Director of the Bureau of Writings.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Bureau of Writings.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon after he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 顧胤者，蘇州吳人也。

translations.literal: Gu Yin was a man of Wu in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yin came from Wu in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖越，陳給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yue was Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gu Yue had served Chen as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 父覽，隋秘書學士。

translations.literal: His father Lan was a Academician of the Secretariat of the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gu Lan had been an Academician of the Sui Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 胤，永徽中歷遷起居郎，兼修國史。

translations.literal: Yin, in the Yonghui reign, was promoted in succession to Diarist, and concurrently compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: During Yonghui, Gu Yin rose through the ranks to Diarist and also took part in compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 撰《太宗實錄》二十捲成，以功加朝散大夫，授弘文館學士。

translations.literal: When he finished compiling the Veritable Record of the Taizong in twenty juan, by merit he was granted Grand Master of the Palace, and appointed Academician of the Hongwen Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When he completed the twenty-juan Veritable Record of Taizong, he was rewarded with the rank of Grand Master of the Palace and appointed an Academician of the Hongwen Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 以撰武德、貞觀兩朝國史八十捲成，加朝請大夫，封餘杭縣男，賜帛五百段。

translations.literal: When he completed compiling the national history of the Wude and Zhenguan reigns in eighty juan, he was granted Gentleman for Court Attendance, enfeoffed as Baron of Yuhang County, and granted five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: After finishing the eighty-juan national history of the Wude and Zhenguan reigns, he was promoted to Gentleman for Court Attendance, enfeoffed as Baron of Yuhang County, and granted five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 龍朔三年，遷司文郎中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Longshuo, he was transferred to be Director of the Bureau of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 3 he was transferred to Director of the Bureau of Literature.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon after he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 胤又撰《漢書古今集》二十捲，行於代。

translations.literal: Yin also compiled the Collection of Ancient and Modern Matters from the Han History in twenty juan, which circulated in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yin also compiled the Collection of Ancient and Modern Matters from the Book of Han in twenty juan, which circulated widely in his time.

sentences.zh: 子琮，長安中為天官侍郎、同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: His son Cong, during the Chang'an era, served as Vice Director of the Bureau of Celestial Officials and Pingzhangshi of the Tong Fengge Luantai.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gu Cong, during the Chang'an period, served as Vice Director of the Bureau of Celestial Officials and as a Chief Minister of the Tong Fengge Luantai.

sentences.zh: 李延壽者，本隴西著姓，世居相州。

translations.literal: Li Yanshou — originally of an eminent Longxi clan name, his family resided in Xiangzhou for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanshou belonged to a distinguished Longxi clan whose family had lived in Xiangzhou for generations.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，累補太子典膳丞、崇賢館學士，嘗受詔與著作佐郎敬播同修《五代史志》，又預撰《晉書》，尋轉御史台主簿，兼直國史。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era, he was repeatedly appointed to Director of the Crown Prince's Victuals Office and Academician of the Chongxian Pavilion; he once received an edict together with Assistant Director of the Bureau of Writings Jing Bo to jointly compile the Annals of the Five Dynasties; he also took part in compiling the Book of Jin; soon he was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Censorate, and concurrently served directly on the national history.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan he served in succession as Director of the Crown Prince's Victuals Office and as an Academician of the Chongxian Pavilion. He was once ordered, together with Assistant Director of the Bureau of Writings Jing Bo, to help compile the Annals of the Five Dynasties, and also took part in drafting the Book of Jin. He was soon transferred to Chief Clerk of the Censorate while continuing to serve on the national history.

sentences.zh: 延壽嘗撰《太宗政典》三十捲表上之。

translations.literal: Yanshou once compiled the Administrative Canons of the Taizong in thirty juan and submitted them in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou once compiled the Administrative Canons of Taizong in thirty juan and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 歷遷符璽郎，兼修國史，尋卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Keeper of the Seals, and concurrently compiled the national history; soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Keeper of the Seals while continuing to compile the national history, and died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 調露中，高宗嘗觀其所撰《政典》，嘆美久之，令藏於秘閣，賜其家帛五十段。

translations.literal: During the Tiaolu reign, the Gaozong once viewed the Administrative Canons he had compiled, sighed in admiration for a long time, ordered it stored in the Secret Pavilion, and granted his family fifty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiaolu era Emperor Gaozong once read the Administrative Canons Yanshou had written, admired them at length, ordered them stored in the Secret Pavilion, and granted his family fifty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 延壽又嘗刪補宋、齊、梁、陳及魏、齊、周、隋等八代史，謂之《南北史》，凡一百八十捲，頗行於代。

translations.literal: Yanshou also once abridged and revised the histories of the Song, Qi, Liang, Chen, Wei, Qi, Zhou, and Sui and other eight dynasties, calling it the History of North and South, one hundred eighty juan in total, and it circulated quite widely in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou also abridged and reworked the histories of the eight dynasties from Song, Qi, Liang, and Chen in the south to Wei, Qi, Zhou, and Sui in the north, producing the History of North and South in one hundred eighty juan, which circulated widely in his time.

sentences.zh: 李仁實，魏州頓丘人。

translations.literal: Li Renshi was a man of Dunqiu in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Renshi came from Dunqiu in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 官至左史。

translations.literal: He reached the office of Left Historiographer.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of Left Historiographer.

sentences.zh: 嘗著《格論》三卷、《通歷》八卷、《戎州記》，並行於時。

translations.literal: He once authored Treatise on Standards in three juan, Comprehensive Chronology in eight juan, and Record of Rongzhou, all of which circulated at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Treatise on Standards in three juan, the Comprehensive Chronology in eight juan, and the Record of Rongzhou, all of which circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 孔穎達，字仲達，冀州衡水人也。

translations.literal: Kong Yingda, style name Zhongda, was a man of Hengshui in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yingda, courtesy name Zhongda, came from Hengshui in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 祖碩，後魏南台丞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shuo was Director of the Southern Bureau of the Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kong Shuo had served the Northern Wei as Director of the Southern Bureau.

sentences.zh: 父安，齊青州法曹參軍。

translations.literal: His father An was Legal Affairs Officer of Qingzhou in the Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kong An had been a Legal Affairs Officer in Qingzhou under the Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 穎達八歲就學，日誦千餘言。

translations.literal: At age eight Yingda began study; each day he recited over a thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: Yingda began his studies at eight and could recite more than a thousand characters a day.

sentences.zh: 及長，尤明《左氏傳》、《鄭氏尚書》、《王氏易》、《毛詩》、《禮記》，兼善算歷，解屬文。

translations.literal: When grown, he was especially versed in the Zuo Commentary, the Book of Documents according to Zheng Xuan, the Changes according to Wang Bi, the Mao Odes, the Book of Rites, and was also skilled in astronomical calculation and calendar science, and adept at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he was especially accomplished in the Zuo Commentary, Zheng Xuan's Book of Documents, Wang Bi's Book of Changes, the Mao Odes, and the Book of Rites, and was also skilled in mathematics and calendrical science and adept at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 同郡劉焯名重海內，穎達造其門。

translations.literal: Liu Zhuo of the same commandery was famed throughout the empire; Yingda went to his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhuo of the same commandery enjoyed a reputation that reached across the empire, and Yingda went to study at his door.

sentences.zh: 焯初不之禮，穎達請質疑滯，多出其意表，焯改容敬之。

translations.literal: At first Zhuo did not treat him with courtesy; Yingda requested to raise questions on points of doubt and confusion, many of which went beyond what Zhuo had expected; Zhuo changed his manner and showed him respect.
translations.idiomatic: At first Liu Zhuo paid him little regard, but when Yingda asked to discuss difficult points, many of his questions went beyond what Zhuo had anticipated, and Zhuo changed his manner and treated him with respect.

sentences.zh: 穎達固辭歸，焯固留不可。

translations.literal: Yingda firmly declined to return; Zhuo firmly tried to detain him but could not.
translations.idiomatic: Yingda insisted on going home, and though Zhuo pressed him to stay, he could not be kept.

sentences.zh: 還家，以教授為務。

translations.literal: Returning home, he made teaching his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Back home, he devoted himself to teaching.

sentences.zh: 隋大業初，舉明經高第，授河內郡博士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye of the Sui, he was recommended in the Mingjing examination with high rank and appointed Doctor of Henei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Daye reign he passed the Mingjing examination with high honors and was appointed Doctor of Henei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 時煬帝征諸郡儒官集於東都，令國子秘書學士與之論難，穎達為最。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Yang summoned the Confucian officials of the various commanderies to assemble at the Eastern Capital, and ordered academicians of the National University and Secretariat to debate with them; Yingda ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang summoned Confucian officials from the commanderies to the Eastern Capital and had academicians of the National University and Secretariat debate with them, Yingda ranked first.

sentences.zh: 時穎達少年，而先輩宿儒恥為之屈，潛遣刺客圖之。

translations.literal: At that time Yingda was young, and senior Confucians of former generations were ashamed to be bested by him, and secretly sent assassins to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: Yingda was still young, and older master scholars, ashamed to be outdone by him, secretly sent assassins against him.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書楊玄感舍之於家，由是獲免。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan kept him at his home, and by this he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuangan, Minister of Rites, took him into his household, and in that way he escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 補太學助教。

translations.literal: He was appointed Assistant Instructor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Assistant Instructor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 屬隋亂，避地於武牢。

translations.literal: When the Sui fell into disorder, he fled to refuge at Wulao.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui empire collapsed into chaos, he took refuge at Wulao.

sentences.zh: 太宗平王世充，引為秦府文學館學士。

translations.literal: When the Taizong pacified Wang Shichong, he was brought in as Academician of the Literary Institute of the Prince of Qin's Mansion.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong defeated Wang Shichong, Yingda was brought into the Prince of Qin's Literary Institute as an academician.

sentences.zh: 武德九年，擢授國子博士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Wude, he was promoted and appointed Doctor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 9 he was promoted to Doctor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，封曲阜縣男，轉給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Qufu County and transferred to Attendant of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhenguan he was enfeoffed as Baron of Qufu County and transferred to the post of Attendant of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時太宗初即位，留心庶政，穎達數進忠言，益見親待。

translations.literal: At that time the Taizong had just ascended the throne and applied his mind to the myriad affairs of government; Yingda several times presented loyal words and was increasingly shown intimate favor.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong had just ascended the throne and was attentive to the business of government; Yingda offered loyal counsel on several occasions and came to be treated with growing favor.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗問曰：「《論語》云：『以能問於不能，以多問於寡，有若無，實若虛。』

translations.literal: The Taizong once asked: "The Analects says: 'The able asking of the unable, the many asking of the few, having as though not having, being full as though empty.'
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once asked, "The Analects says, 'Let the able ask of the unable; let the many ask of the few; possess as though one possessed nothing; be full as though one were empty.'

sentences.zh: 何謂也？」

translations.literal: What does this mean?"
translations.idiomatic: What does this mean?"

sentences.zh: 穎達對曰：「聖人設教，欲人謙光。

translations.literal: Yingda replied: "The sage establishes teaching, desiring that people be humble and modest.
translations.idiomatic: Yingda replied, "The sage established his teaching to make men humble and self-effacing.

sentences.zh: 己雖有能，不自矜大，仍就不能之人求訪能事。

translations.literal: Though one already has ability, one does not self-aggrandize; still one seeks out matters of ability from those without ability.
translations.idiomatic: Though one already has ability, one does not boast of it, but still seeks instruction from those who seem less capable.

sentences.zh: 己之才藝雖多，猶以為少，仍就寡少之人更求所益。

translations.literal: Though one's talents and arts are many, one still considers them few; still one goes to those with few and seeks further benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Though one's talents are many, one still treats them as insufficient and goes to those who seem to have little in order to gain more.

sentences.zh: 己之雖有，其狀若無。

translations.literal: Though one has possessions, one's appearance is as though one has none.
translations.idiomatic: Though one possesses much, one appears as though one possessed nothing.

sentences.zh: 己之雖實，其容若虛。

translations.literal: Though one is full, one's bearing is as though empty.
translations.idiomatic: Though one is full, one's bearing is as though one were empty.

sentences.zh: 非唯匹庶，帝王之德，亦當如此。

translations.literal: It is not only common people — the virtue of an emperor should also be like this.
translations.idiomatic: This applies not only to common people; the virtue of an emperor should be the same.

sentences.zh: 夫帝王內蘊神明，外須玄默，使深不可測，度不可知。

translations.literal: An emperor inwardly contains divine wisdom, but outwardly must be dark and silent, so that the depths cannot be fathomed and his measure cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler should harbor divine insight within while outwardly remaining reserved and still, so that his depths cannot be fathomed and his intentions cannot be read.

sentences.zh: 《易》稱『以蒙養正，以明夷蒞眾』，若其位居尊極，炫耀聰明，以才凌人，飾非拒諫，則上下情隔，君臣道乖。

translations.literal: The Changes says 'By obscurity one nurtures righteousness; by Brightness Hidden one presides over the multitude.' If one occupies the supreme position and displays one's brilliance, uses talent to dominate others, adorns faults and rejects remonstrance, then sentiment is blocked between high and low and the Way between sovereign and minister is sundered.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, 'By obscurity one nurtures what is right; by Brightness Hidden one governs the multitude.' If a ruler in the highest place flaunts his brilliance, uses talent to dominate others, covers his faults, and rejects remonstrance, feeling is cut off between high and low and the bond between sovereign and minister is broken.

sentences.zh: 自古滅亡，莫不由此也。」

translations.literal: Since ancient times, none have perished without this cause."
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, no dynasty has fallen except by this path."

sentences.zh: 太宗深善其對。

translations.literal: The Taizong deeply approved of his answer.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was deeply pleased with his answer.

sentences.zh: 六年，累除國子司業。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was successively removed and appointed Vice Director of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed Vice Director of the National University.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，遷太子右庶子，仍兼國子司業。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince, still concurrently Vice Director of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a year he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince while retaining his post as Vice Director of the National University.

sentences.zh: 與諸儒議歷及明堂，皆從穎達之說。

translations.literal: In discussions with the various Confucians on the calendar and the Bright Hall, all followed Yingda's views.
translations.idiomatic: When the court scholars debated the calendar and the Bright Hall, all followed Yingda's views.

sentences.zh: 又與魏徵撰成《隋史》，加位散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He also together with Wei Zheng completed compiling the History of Sui, and his rank was elevated to Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He also helped Wei Zheng complete the History of Sui and was promoted to Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 十一年，又與朝賢修定《五禮》，所有疑滯，咸諮決之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he also together with court worthies revised and fixed the Five Rites; wherever there were doubts and blockages, all were referred to Yingda for decision.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he joined court worthies in revising the Five Rites, and every doubtful point was referred to Yingda for final decision.

sentences.zh: 書成，進爵為子，賜物三百段。

translations.literal: When the book was completed, he was advanced in noble rank to Viscount and granted three hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, he was raised to the rank of Viscount and granted three hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 庶人承乾令撰《孝經義疏》，穎達因文見意，更廣規諷之道，學者稱之。

translations.literal: The commoner Chengan ordered him to compile Exegesis of the Classic of Filial Piety; Yingda, through the text, conveyed his meaning and further broadened the way of indirect admonition; scholars praised it.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed heir Chengan ordered him to compile an exegesis of the Classic of Filial Piety, Yingda read meaning through the text and broadened the path of indirect remonstrance; scholars praised the work.

sentences.zh: 太宗以穎達在東宮數有匡諫，與左庶子於志寧各賜黃金一斤、絹百匹。

translations.literal: The Taizong, because Yingda in the Eastern Palace had several times offered corrective remonstrance, together with Left Vice Director Yu Zhining each granted one jin of yellow gold and a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yingda had repeatedly offered corrective remonstrance in the Eastern Palace, Taizong granted him and Left Vice Director Yu Zhining each one jin of gold and a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 十二年，拜國子祭酒，仍侍講東宮。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he was appointed Chancellor of the National University, and still lectured at the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was appointed Chancellor of the National University while continuing to lecture in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 十四年，太宗幸國學觀釋奠，命穎達講《孝經》，既畢，穎達上《釋奠頌》，手詔褒美。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, the Taizong visited the National University to observe the sacrifice of the first harvest; he ordered Yingda to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety; when finished, Yingda submitted an Ode for the Sacrifice of the First Harvest, and the Emperor personally wrote an edict praising and commending him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Taizong visited the National University for the harvest sacrifice, ordered Yingda to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, and when the lecture was done Yingda submitted an Ode for the Sacrifice; the emperor answered with a personal edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 後承乾不循法度，穎達每犯顏進諫。

translations.literal: Afterwards Chengan did not follow laws and standards; Yingda each time risked offense to offer remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Chengan ignored proper conduct, Yingda repeatedly risked giving offense to remonstrate with him directly.

sentences.zh: 承乾乳母遂安夫人謂曰：「太子成長，何宜屢致面折？」

translations.literal: Chengan's wet nurse Lady Suian said to him: "The Crown Prince has grown up — how is it fitting repeatedly to bring about direct rebuke to his face?"
translations.idiomatic: Chengan's wet nurse, Lady Suian, said to him, "The Crown Prince is grown — why must you rebuke him to his face again and again?"

sentences.zh: 穎達對曰：「蒙國厚恩，死無所恨。」

translations.literal: Yingda replied: "Having received the state's thick grace, in death I have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: Yingda replied, "I have received the state's great favor; if I die in the course of duty, I shall have no regret."

sentences.zh: 諫諍逾切，承乾不能納。

translations.literal: His remonstrance became ever more urgent; Chengan could not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: His remonstrance grew ever sharper, and Chengan would not heed it.

sentences.zh: 先是，與顏師古、司馬才章、王恭、王琰等諸儒受詔撰定《五經》義訓，凡一百八十捲，名曰《五經正義》。

translations.literal: Previously, together with Yan Shigu, Sima Caizhang, Wang Gong, Wang Yan, and other Confucians, he received an edict to compile and fix the exegetical glosses of the Five Classics, one hundred eighty juan in total, entitled Correct Meanings of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, together with Yan Shigu, Sima Caizhang, Wang Gong, Wang Yan, and other scholars, he had received an edict to compile authoritative glosses on the Five Classics — one hundred eighty juan in all, entitled the Correct Meanings of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 太宗下詔曰：「卿等博綜古今，義理該洽，考前儒之異說，符聖人之幽旨，實為不朽。」

translations.literal: The Taizong issued an edict saying: "You have broadly mastered ancient and modern, your principles are comprehensive and harmonious, you have examined the differing theories of earlier Confucians and accord with the sage's subtle intent — this is truly work that will not perish."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong issued an edict saying, "You have mastered ancient and modern learning, your principles are comprehensive and sound, you have weighed the differing views of earlier scholars and accord with the sage's deepest intent — this is work that will endure."

sentences.zh: 付國子監施行，賜穎達物三百段。

translations.literal: It was delivered to the Directorate of the National University for implementation, and Yingda was granted three hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The text was ordered put into use at the Directorate of Education, and Yingda was granted three hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 時又有太學博士馬嘉運駁穎達所撰《正義》，詔更令詳定，功竟未就。

translations.literal: At that time there was also Doctor of the Imperial Academy Ma Jiayun who refuted the Correct Meanings Yingda had compiled; an edict ordered further detailed revision, but the work was ultimately not completed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ma Jiayun, a Doctor of the Imperial Academy, challenged the Correct Meanings Yingda had compiled; an edict ordered further revision, but the work was never finished.

sentences.zh: 十七年，以年老致仕。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, because of old age he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he retired from office on account of age.

sentences.zh: 十八年，圖形於凌煙閣，贊曰：「道光列第，風傳闕裡。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, his portrait was painted in the Lingyan Pavilion; the encomium read: "The Way's light ranks among the mansions; the wind of learning spreads through the tower gates of the academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year his portrait was placed in the Lingyan Pavilion; the encomium read, "His Way illumined the halls of learning; the wind of his teaching spread from the academy gates.

sentences.zh: 精義霞開，掞辭飈起。」

translations.literal: Profound meanings open like rosy clouds; polished phrasing rises like a gale."
translations.idiomatic: Profound meanings opened like dawn clouds; polished words rose like a rushing wind."

sentences.zh: 二十二年卒，陪葬昭陵，贈太常卿，謚曰憲。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he died, was buried with honor at Zhaoling, was posthumously granted Minister of Rites, and his posthumous title was Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-second year, was buried with honor at Zhaoling, was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites, and given the posthumous name Xian.

sentences.zh: 司馬才章者，魏州貴鄉人也。

translations.literal: Sima Caizhang was a man of Guixiang in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Caizhang came from Guixiang in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 父烜，博涉《五經》，善緯候。

translations.literal: His father Xuan was broadly versed in the Five Classics and skilled in wei and hou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sima Xuan was broadly versed in the Five Classics and skilled in apocryphal and omen lore.

sentences.zh: 才章少傳其業。

translations.literal: Caizhang in youth transmitted his father's craft.
translations.idiomatic: Caizhang inherited his father's learning from youth.

sentences.zh: 隋末為郡博士，貞觀六年，左僕射房玄齡薦之，屢蒙召問，擢授國子助教，論議該洽，學者稱之。

translations.literal: At the end of the Sui he was a commandery doctor; in the sixth year of Zhenguan, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Fang Xuanling recommended him; he repeatedly received summons for questioning; he was promoted and appointed Assistant Instructor of the Imperial Academy; his discourse was comprehensive and harmonious, and scholars praised him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui he served as a commandery doctor. In Zhenguan 6 the Left Vice Director Fang Xuanling recommended him; he was repeatedly summoned for questioning, promoted to Assistant Instructor of the Imperial Academy, and praised by scholars for the breadth and soundness of his discourse.

sentences.zh: 王恭者，滑州白馬人也。

translations.literal: Wang Gong was a man of Baima in Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong came from Baima in Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 少篤學，博涉《六經》。

translations.literal: In youth he was devoted to learning and broadly versed in the Six Classics.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was devoted to learning and broadly versed in the Six Classics.

sentences.zh: 每於鄉閭教授，弟子自遠方至數百人。

translations.literal: Whenever he taught in the villages and hamlets, disciples came from afar, numbering several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: When he taught in the countryside, disciples came from afar until their number reached several hundred.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，征拜太學博士，其所講《三禮》，皆別立義證，甚為精博。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, he was summoned and appointed Doctor of the Imperial Academy; the Three Rituals he lectured on each had separately established textual proofs, which were very refined and comprehensive.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenguan years he was summoned as Doctor of the Imperial Academy; in his lectures on the Three Rituals he developed separate textual proofs of his own, and his learning was exceptionally deep and broad.

sentences.zh: 蓋文懿、文達等皆當時大儒，罕所推借，每講《三禮》，皆遍舉先達義，而亦暢恭所說。

translations.literal: Gai Wenyi, Wenda and others were all great Confucians of the time, rarely granting approval to others; whenever they lectured on the Three Rituals, they all cited comprehensively the meanings of earlier masters, and also fully expounded what Gong had said.
translations.idiomatic: Gai Wenyi, Wenda, and others were leading scholars of the day who rarely conceded merit to anyone else; yet whenever they lectured on the Three Rituals they cited the interpretations of earlier masters in full and also gave free rein to what Gong had taught.

sentences.zh: 馬嘉運者，魏州繁水人也。

translations.literal: Ma Jiayun was a man of Fenshui in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jiayun came from Fenshui in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 少出家為沙門，明於《三論》。

translations.literal: In youth he left home to become a monk and was accomplished in the Three Treatises.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the monkhood in youth and mastered the Three Treatises school of Buddhist thought.

sentences.zh: 後更還俗，專精儒業，尤善論難。

translations.literal: Later he again returned to lay life, devoted himself exclusively to Confucian studies, and was especially skilled at debate.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned to lay life, devoted himself to Confucian learning, and was especially adept at scholastic debate.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，累除越王東閣祭酒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, he was repeatedly appointed libationer at the Eastern Pavilion of the Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenguan years he rose through successive appointments as libationer at the Eastern Pavilion of the Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 頃之，罷歸，隱居白鹿山。

translations.literal: Before long he was dismissed and returned home, living in seclusion on Mount Bailu.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was dismissed and retired, living in seclusion on Mount Bailu.

sentences.zh: 十一年，召拜太學博士，兼弘文館學士，預修《文思博要》。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was summoned and appointed Doctor of the Imperial Academy, concurrently Academician of the Hongwen Pavilion, and took part in compiling the Literary Mind and Broad Essentials.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was summoned as Doctor of the Imperial Academy and also made a scholar of the Hongwen Pavilion, joining the compilation of the Literary Mind and Broad Essentials.

sentences.zh: 嘉運以穎達所撰《正義》頗多繁雜，每掎摭之，諸儒亦稱為允當。

translations.literal: Jiayun considered the Correct Meanings that Yingda had compiled to be in many places cumbersome and redundant, and frequently picked out its flaws; the various Confucians also declared his criticisms fair.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayun found Kong Yingda's Correct Meanings often cumbersome and redundant, and regularly challenged its passages; other scholars agreed that his criticisms were sound.

sentences.zh: 高宗居春宮，引為崇賢館學士。

translations.literal: When Gaozong resided in the Eastern Palace, he was brought in as Academician of the Chongxian Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong served as crown prince, Jiayun was appointed a scholar of the Chongxian Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 數與洗馬秦暐侍講殿中，甚蒙禮異。

translations.literal: He repeatedly lectured in the hall together with Reader Qin Wei and was greatly favored with special courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He often lectured in the palace alongside the Reader Qin Wei and received exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 十九年，遷國子博士卒。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was transferred to Doctor of the National University and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was promoted to Doctor of the National University and died in office.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：唐德勃興，英儒間出，佐命協力，實有其人。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Tang virtue rose powerfully; eminent Confucians emerged one after another; in assisting the mandate and working together, there truly were such men.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: As the Tang dynasty rose in virtue, eminent scholars appeared in succession—men who truly aided the founding effort and worked in concert.

sentences.zh: 薛收左右厥猷，經謀雅道，不幸短命，殲我良士。

translations.literal: Xue Shou guided the foundation plans and counseled on refined principles; unhappily cut short in life, he took from us a fine worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Shou helped shape great plans and advised on the finer points of statecraft; cut short in life, he was a worthy man the dynasty could ill afford to lose.

sentences.zh: 上言「恨不圖形，若在，當以中書令處之」，才可知矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I regret that his likeness was not painted; if he were still alive, I would place him in the post of Director of the Secretariat"—from this his talent may be known.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said, "I regret we never painted his portrait; if he were still alive, I would have made him director of the Secretariat"—from that remark alone his talent is evident.

sentences.zh: 元敬藻翰明敏，而畏權勢，竟不狎房、杜，深沉至慎，不亦優哉！

translations.literal: Yuanjing's literary brush was bright and keen, yet he feared power and influence and in the end did not become intimate with Fang and Du; deeply reserved and extremely cautious—is this not superior!
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing's prose was brilliant and quick, yet he feared power and never grew close to Fang and Du; deeply reserved and cautious to the end—was that not the wiser course?

sentences.zh: 元超藉父風望，弼亮宏略，諒非其罪，而再遷流。

translations.literal: Yuanchao relied on his father's reputation and wind, assisted and illuminated great strategy; surely it was not his crime, yet he was twice transferred to exile.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchao inherited his father's prestige and served the throne with broad vision; his punishments were scarcely deserved, yet he was exiled twice.

sentences.zh: 及登大任，益有嘉謀，汲引多才，以隆弘納，其感恩之重，時其聞諸？

translations.literal: When he reached great responsibility, he all the more had fine counsel, drew up many talents, and thereby elevated broad recruitment; the weight of his gratitude—who in his time has heard the like?
translations.idiomatic: Once restored to high office, he offered still finer counsel and brought forward many talents to broaden imperial recruitment; such depth of gratitude—has any age heard its like?

sentences.zh: 有始有卒，其殆庶幾乎！

translations.literal: Having a beginning and having an end—he perhaps nearly achieved it!
translations.idiomatic: To begin well and finish well—he very nearly achieved that ideal!

sentences.zh: 稷出自名家，涉於大用，及自貽謀釁，如貞亮何？

translations.literal: Ji came from an eminent house and reached great employment; yet when he himself brought on a scheme and strife, what of faithful integrity?
translations.idiomatic: Ji came from a distinguished family and rose to great responsibility, yet when his own plotting brought ruin, what became of his integrity?

sentences.zh: 姚思廉篤學寡慾，受漢史於家尊，果執明義，臨大節而不可奪。

translations.literal: Yao Silian was deeply devoted to learning and few in desires; he received the Han history from his honored father at home; steadfastly he held to clear rightness, and faced great principle without being swayed.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Silian was a devoted scholar of few desires who inherited his father's work on the Book of Han; steadfast in principle, he could not be moved when the stakes were highest.

sentences.zh: 及筆削成書，箴規翊聖，言其命世，亦當仁乎！

translations.literal: When his brush corrections finished the book, he admonished and counseled to assist the sage; to speak of a talent of the age—should this not also be "when there is benevolence, none should defer to him"?
translations.idiomatic: When his editorial labor produced a finished work, he used it to admonish and guide the throne; if ever a man was born for his age, surely he was such a one!

sentences.zh: 師古家籍儒風，該博經義，至於詳註史策，探測典禮，清明在躬，天有才格。

translations.literal: Shigu's house was rooted in Confucian wind; comprehensively broad in classical meaning; as for annotating historical records in detail and probing ceremonial ritual—clarity and illumination were in his person; Heaven had given him a pattern of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu came from a scholarly family and mastered the classics; in annotating history and probing ritual, clarity lived in his person—Heaven had marked him as a man of talent.

sentences.zh: 然而三黜之負，竟在時譏，孔子曰「才難」，不其然乎？

translations.literal: Yet the burden of three dismissals was ultimately a mark of ridicule in his time; Confucius said "talent is hard to find"—is it not so?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the stain of three demotions drew the ridicule of his age; as Confucius said, "Talent is hard to find"—was he not right?

sentences.zh: 令狐德棻貞度應時，待問平直。

translations.literal: Linghu Defen had upright measure fitted to the times; in awaiting inquiries he was direct and even.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Defen was upright and attuned to his age, candid and fair in answering every question put to him.

sentences.zh: 征舊史，修新禮，以暢國風；

translations.literal: He summoned old histories and revised the new ritual, thereby giving full expression to national style;
translations.idiomatic: He gathered old chronicles and restored new ritual, letting the spirit of the age flow freely;

sentences.zh: 辨治亂，談王霸，以資帝業。

translations.literal: He distinguished order and disorder, discussed kingly and hegemonic rule, thereby supplying resources for the imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: he weighed order against chaos and counseled on rule by virtue and by force, thereby furnishing the foundations of empire.

sentences.zh: 「元首明哉，股肱良哉」，其斯之謂歟！

translations.literal: "The head is enlightened indeed; the limbs are excellent indeed"—does this refer to such men!
translations.idiomatic: "The sovereign is wise, and his ministers are worthy"—such praise was surely meant for men like these!

sentences.zh: 鄧世隆國史時譽，固有諒直。

translations.literal: Deng Shilong had timely reputation in the national history and indeed possessed understanding and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Shilong won timely praise for his work on the national history and was genuinely candid and upright.

sentences.zh: 其覆書不遜，何不知之甚也！

translations.literal: That his reply letter was not deferential—how very lacking in judgment!
translations.idiomatic: Yet that his reply was defiant—how profoundly he misjudged the moment!

sentences.zh: 上疏請編御集，其弼直乎！

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial requesting compilation of the imperial collection—is this not assisting and being upright!
translations.idiomatic: His memorial asking that the emperor's writings be compiled and preserved—that was true ministerial candor!

sentences.zh: 顧胤清芬，可觀彝范，積善餘慶，其有子哉！

translations.literal: Gu Yin had a pure fragrance, worthy to be viewed as a constant model; the surplus blessing of accumulated goodness—did he not have a son!
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yin left a pure reputation and a model worth emulating; the blessing of accumulated virtue lived on—did he not have a worthy son?

sentences.zh: 李延壽研考史學，修撰刪補，克成大典，方之班、馬，何代無人？

translations.literal: Li Yanshou examined and studied historical learning, compiled, edited, and supplemented, and succeeded in completing a great canon; compared with Ban and Sima—what age lacks such men?
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanshou studied historiography deeply, revised, edited, and supplemented his work until he produced a great historical compilation; compared with Ban Gu and Sima Qian, has any age truly lacked men of such caliber?

sentences.zh: 仁實據摭，抑又次焉。

translations.literal: Renshi compiled by gleaning; yet he ranks still lower.
translations.idiomatic: Li Renshi merely compiled by excerpting, and ranks still farther below.

sentences.zh: 孔穎達風格高爽，幼而有聞，探賾明敏，辨析應對，天有通才。

translations.literal: Kong Yingda's style was lofty and open; he had fame even in youth; probing the profound he was bright and keen; in analysis and response—Heaven had given a universal talent.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yingda was lofty in bearing and famed even as a youth; penetrating in analysis and quick in debate, Heaven had endowed him with universal talent.

sentences.zh: 人道惡盈，必有毀訐，及《正義》炳煥，乃異人也，雖其掎摭，亦何損於明？

translations.literal: Human way hates fullness; there must be slander and denunciation; yet when the Correct Meanings shone brilliantly he was nevertheless an extraordinary man; though there were those who picked at it, what did that harm in brightness?
translations.idiomatic: Human nature resents excellence, and calumny inevitably follows; yet when the Correct Meanings shone in brilliance, Yingda stood apart as an extraordinary man; though critics picked at his work, what did that diminish his clarity?

sentences.zh: 司馬才章藉時崇儒，明核致業；

translations.literal: Sima Caizhang relied on the times' elevation of Confucian learning, clearly verified and achieved his work;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Caizhang seized the age's reverence for learning and achieved his work through clear-eyed scholarship;

sentences.zh: 王恭弘闡聲教，禮學研詳；

translations.literal: Wang Gong broadly expounded sound instruction, and with ritual learning research was thorough;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong spread the civilizing teaching and studied ritual learning in painstaking detail;

sentences.zh: 馬嘉運達識自通，克成典雅。

translations.literal: Ma Jiayun had penetrating knowledge and was naturally accomplished, and succeeded in completing elegant correctness.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jiayun possessed penetrating insight and native mastery, and brought elegance to completion.

sentences.zh: 並符才用，潤色丹青，其掎摭繁雜，蓋求備者也。

translations.literal: All accorded with talent and employment, embellishing like cinnabar and green; their picking out redundancy and complexity—this was perhaps seeking completeness.
translations.idiomatic: All were men whose talents matched their task, adding polish like pigment to a painting; when they picked out redundant passages, it was surely in pursuit of thoroughness.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：河東三鳳，俱瑞黃圖。

translations.literal: Encomium says: The Three Phoenixes of Hedong—all auspicious omens in the Yellow Map.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: The Three Phoenixes of Hedong—all propitious signs within the imperial capital.

sentences.zh: 棻為良史，穎實名儒。

translations.literal: Fen was a fine historiographer; Ying was truly a famed Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: Defen was the fine historian; Yingda was the renowned classicist.

sentences.zh: 解經不窮，希顏之徒。

translations.literal: Unceasing in explicating the classics—they are of the company of those who aspire to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In interpreting the classics they never reached the end—they were men in the lineage of those who aspire to Yan Hui.

sentences.zh: 登瀛入館，不其盛乎！

translations.literal: Ascending to the isles and entering the pavilion—is this not glorious!
translations.idiomatic: To ascend to Penglai and enter the Academy—is not that a glory unmatched!
